detail.abstract: This paper studies whether the value of expert testimony lies primarily in informational content or in the institutional role of the expert witness. We first develop a screening model in which AI compresses differences in methodological production and shifts judicial evaluation toward institutional signals. Using federal district court Daubert opinions in copyright cases, we compare observed expert packages with AI-generated packages from neutralized case descriptions. AI substantially reproduces the legal and evidentiary objectives served by retained expert testimony, with stronger alignment for accepted testimony than for excluded testimony. When the AI package covers more of what the retained expert actually needed to address, courts are less likely to exclude the testimony. These results continue to hold after robustness tests addressing case-name leakage, generic template generation, output length, and model dependence. This suggests that as expert methodology becomes easier to reproduce, admissibility may depend increasingly on institutional features such as qualifications.

detail.abstract: As the population ages, the development of effective public policies for elderly care has become increasingly relevant. Using a difference-indifferences approach, we assess the effects of public elderly care centers in Brazil on the labor market outcomes of family members. The results indicate that the opening of these centers is associated with a 1.49% increase in the probability of formal employment and a 4.32% increase in average income. Despite the larger effect of the probability of formal employment among women, income gains are observed only among men. These findings underscore the importance of expanding access to formal elderly care services to improve labor market outcomes and may reduce some gender disparities.

detail.abstract: Students increasingly use generative artificial intelligence (AI) to prepare for economics examinations using published questions and scoring rubrics. Using AP Microeconomics and Macroeconomics questions, we examine whether disclosing grading criteria, reallocating points, or omitting criteria affects the correctness of AI-generated answers. Providing the complete rubric increases correctness from 74.0% to 75.6%, a statistically insignificant difference. Reallocating points reduces correctness by only 0.17 percentage points, while omitting a criterion does not cause AI to neglect the corresponding question requirement. Even with the complete rubric, AI addresses 99.2% of required components but fully satisfies only 75.6%. For economics educators, these findings suggest that detailed rubrics neither reliably improve AI-generated explanations nor produce detectable harmful responses to grading incentives. More importantly, comprehensive answers may still contain substantive economic errors.

detail.abstract: Who disciplines managers when trade protection shields them from competition? We exploit the 2018-19 U.S. tariffs as a shock to import competition and show that hedge fund activists become more likely to target firms in protected industries, particularly recent outperformers and firms facing little domestic competition. These campaigns more often demand board seats and governance changes, lead to more new director appointments, and generate abnormal returns of 15%, more than double those of similar campaigns before the tariffs. Untargeted protected firms become more profitable, grow their assets, and cut R&D; targets instead raise R&D and repurchases and slow their asset growth. Activism, but not internal governance or the market for corporate control, substitutes for the competitive discipline loosened by protection.

detail.abstract: Contemporary central bank communication focuses predominantly on delivering forward guidance to specialized audiences, notably financial market analysts and large corporate enterprises. For wage-earning households and small businesses, this orientation leaves a pronounced informational gap. Because non-specialist agents tend to form beliefs through backward-looking, localized price experiences, they often require retrospective explanation, or what we term backward guidance, to interpret macroeconomic developments. Beyond individual cognitive constraints, we argue that this informational asymmetry reflects differences in production-network breadth and institutional proximity. Operating across multi-tiered value chains allows large firms to assemble a coherent forecast of future cost and demand conditions from a mosaic of upstream supplier quotes, logistics indicators, and downstream order books, while their macroeconomic footprint affords recurring consultative access to policy institutions. Small retail or service enterprises and ordinary consumers lack these linkages. A persistent Expectational Wedge (∆E t ≡ E f t [π t+1 ]-E h t [π t+1 ])

detail.abstract: Governments promote STEM education to raise productivity and narrow gender gaps. We develop a general-equilibrium life-cycle model with major choice, career choice, and endogenous innovation to evaluate such policies. A moderate STEM expansion increases welfare and growth, but further expansion draws students from better-fitting majors and reduces research capacity. At similar costs, general tuition aid yields the largest welfare gain, while STEM subsidy delivers the largest growth response. Female-targeted STEM policy increases women's representation and narrows the earnings gap, but heavy targeting lowers welfare. Education aid can also outperform direct R&D subsidies by expanding researcher supply and reducing labor costs.

detail.abstract: We show empirically that the reallocation of employment from manufacturing to services in the U.S. was driven by large incumbent service firms, which expanded by opening additional establishments. Guided by these facts, we develop a two-sector general equilibrium model of firm dynamics in which incumbent firms can scale by operating multiple establishments. Quantitatively, a relative increase in manufacturing productivity and a decline in replication costs-the cost of opening and managing additional establishments-jointly account for more than half of the observed sectoral reallocation. The productivity channel shifts employment toward services but leaves the firm-size distribution unchanged. Lower replication costs, by contrast, generate the disproportionate expansion of large, multi-establishment service firms and, on their own, account for roughly one third of the reallocation generated by the two forces jointly. Our results identify firm dynamics-specifically, incumbent expansion through new establishments-as a quantitatively important force behind structural transformation.

detail.abstract: Platforms can use recommendation algorithms to steer consumers toward more profitable items at the expense of consumer welfare. Proposals such as in-situ data rights would let consumers choose between a platform's own algorithm and third-party algorithms. Such competition can discipline platforms only if consumers recognize which algorithm serves them better and value it accordingly. I test this premise in a pre-registered online experiment. I elicit subjects’ risk preferences and use them to rank lotteries with two personalized algorithms: one maximizes the subject’s expected utility, the other also minimizes the platform’s expected cost. This platform algorithm lowers the certainty equivalent of chosen lotteries by $0.42 per choice. Subjects detect the better algorithm and have a positive willingness-to-pay for it on average, but willingness-to-pay is not explained by how much a subject gains from the better algorithm. Choice-based remedies may therefore need to be paired with information about what algorithms optimize. For platforms, better recommendations could serve to differentiate from competitors or be sold as a premium service.

detail.abstract: We study dynamic portfolio choice when investors learn a latent emissions rate from biased and noisy cumulative reports. The model distinguishes the current physical rate from the amount accumulated over each reporting interval and separates additive bias, multiplicative bias, and measurement noise. An exact Gaussian interval filter supplies the observable state for the control problem. Even a noiseless cumulative report generally leaves uncertainty about the current rate. With independent return and emissions shocks, we establish optimality of a constrained quadratic allocation rule at every finite horizon. With linked shocks, an unconstrained feedback follows from a Riccati system with report-date updates, subject to stated verification conditions. A public-data implementation combines national inventories, an external emissions database, and country exchange traded fund returns. A separate Canada-France stress experiment evaluates reporting misspecification under a common welfare criterion. Starting from a common calibrated prior, with relative risk aversion two, overlooking hypothetical 20% Canadian underreporting at a unit noise-tosignal variance ratio increases the thirty-year mean time-averaged Canadian weight by 5.97 percentage points and simulated carbon exposure by 11.39%. The wealth-equivalent loss is 0.30% for ignored bias, 0.60% for ignored bias and noise jointly, and 2.24% under a severe joint stress. Reporting noise can be costly even when average allocations barely change.

detail.abstract: Introduction: Workforce Compliance is an Investment Risk Nigeria offers substantial investment opportunities across energy, infrastructure, manufacturing, financial services, technology, real estate, and consumer markets. However, establishing or expanding a business in Nigeria involves more than obtaining corporate registration, securing permits, and committing capital. Investors must also understand and manage the employment, immigration, labour, and statutory obligations that arise from engaging a workforce. Workforce non-compliance can expose a business to contractual claims, regulatory sanctions, immigration complications, unpaid employee entitlements, industrial disputes, project delays, and reputational damage. These risks become particularly significant during mergers and acquisitions, large-scale construction projects, workforce restructuring, and the deployment of expatriate personnel.

detail.abstract: The Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM), launched by the Government of India in October 2014, is one of the largest sanitation programmes ever undertaken, aiming to eliminate open defecation and improve solid waste management nationwide. In the years since, SBM has been described in strikingly different terms depending on who is doing the describing. This project asks a specific question about that disagreement: does the way SBM is discussed differ in measurable, systematic ways depending on the type of source doing the discussing, and depending on which stakeholder group a given piece of writing is centrally about? To answer this, I built a 55-document corpus of English-language material on SBM spanning seven source types, hand-coded each document by the stakeholder groups it concerns, and analysed the corpus in Python using VADER sentiment scoring and Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling. Because each document is represented by a summary rather than its full text, the results should be read as descriptive and preliminary. Sentiment differs systematically by source type: government press releases, policy briefings, and NGO reports are mildly positive, while investigative journalism and opinion writing are clearly negative (Mann-Whitney U = 107.5, p = 0.009), with academic papers close to neutral. At the stakeholder level, marginalized castes, the general public, and sanitation workers are framed most negatively. Within the sanitation-worker documents, however, sentiment splits sharply by source: official and parliamentary reports of worker deaths score near neutral or even positive, while advocacy and investigative accounts of the same deaths score strongly negative. The paper also documents a validity problem found during the analysis: an earlier version of the corpus summaries contained my own research notes, which the sentiment model scored as part of the text. Removing them changed several results, a caution for any study that applies sentiment analysis to researcher-prepared text.

detail.abstract: This paper explains how weak institutions make in-group help and out-group exclusion privately beneficial when cultural distance prevents cooperation. Under weak institutions, no external authority reliably protects groups' control over resources. When cooperation gains cannot cover cultural learning costs, groups allocate labor between production and resource contests. With equal sharing among a fixed set of members, restoring a fellow member's labor capacity increases output and resource control. Reducing an outsider's labor capacity weakens a competitor, increasing resource control and releasing labor for production. Both actions raise the actor's income, whereas helping outsiders lowers it. When cooperation gains cover learning costs, joint production makes help beneficial across groups and exclusion costly to the actor. When the initial marginal cost of helping is sufficiently low, these private benefits translate into actual contributions.

detail.abstract: National strategies for artificial intelligence (AI) are usually compared by the resources they mobilise: researchers, research budgets, private investment and computing infrastructure. Far less is known about how efficiently those resources are converted into AI capability, and why conversion differs among countries with comparable endowments. This article operationalises a three-layer view of national AI capability (invention, industrialisation and operationalisation) and measures conversion ratios for China, Japan and South Korea between 2017 and 2025, using the United States as the frontier reference. The analysis combines model-level data from Epoch AI, bibliometric data from OpenAlex, input indicators from the World Bank, investment, patent and diffusion data from the Stanford AI Index 2026, and pillar scores from the Government AI Readiness Index 2025. Three findings stand out. First, Japan is the lowestconverting case in almost every link: it produced 52 AI models in nine years against 87 for South Korea, despite larger research, R&D and compute endowments, and its computeweighted conversion is an order of magnitude below that of its neighbours. Second, the Japanese gap lies in the knowledge-to-model and compute-to-model links, not in the capital link. Third, conversion aligns more closely with the state's policy capacity than with infrastructure or sector maturity: Japan and South Korea score almost identically on development and diffusion, but 70 versus 96 on policy capacity. The results are robust to fractional counting and compute weighting. The article argues that AI sovereignty is a problem of governing conversion, not only of accumulating inputs.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between corporate dividend growth and aggregate output in the United States from 1950 to 2024. I model the aggregate nonfinancial corporate sector as a system in which managers smooth the aggregate return on equity (AROE) around its market-clearing hurdle rate. Because equity is the most expensive funding source, undistributed profits inflate the balance-sheet denominator. Under market saturation and a decaying marginal product of capital, this hoarding creates an overcapitalization trap that dilutes corporate yields. This trap is a manifestation of the law of diminishing marginal returns: as capital accumulates inside mature firms without new investment opportunities, its marginal product falls below the cost of equity. The paper shows how the corporate sector escapes this constraint-not by finding new opportunities within the same firms, but by draining capital out of them and reallocating it to firms where the marginal product is higher. Empirically, I find a pronounced bifurcation. Aggregate profit growth is statistically indistinguishable from noise with respect to real GDP (t = 0.06), and its first lag suppresses growth (-0.061, t =-3.01 for GVA). Real dividend growth, by contrast, is positively and significantly associated with output (+0.321, t = 4.24 for GVA; +0.213, t = 3.53 for GDP), even after controlling for profit growth. The evidence suggests that institutional investors, not managers, are the initiating party in payout decisions. Managers execute within constraints set by investors who have alternative uses for capital. The dividend is the mechanism through which ownership and allocation are reconciled. The reallocation is directed: capital flows from firms whose relative market share has plateaued to firms whose relative market share is expanding. The contemporaneous association between dividends and output is its empirical signature.

detail.abstract: This study provides comprehensive empirical validation and quantitative stress-testing for Part III of the International Integrated Clearing and Settlement System (IICSS), an output-pegged Multi-CBDC Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) framework. While normative mechanism design establishes the theoretical feasibility of suppressing ex-nihilo credit expansion and executing global cross-border clearing, transitioning such architectures to physical deployment requires evaluating civil grid energy vulnerabilities, multi-medium telecommunication severance, and hegemonic hash-power concentration risks. Integrating Monte Carlo stochastic net present value (NPV) optimizations across 10,000 iterations, continuous-time Markov Chain state-space transition modeling, and Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) threshold analysis, we evaluate the system's operational viability under severe physical shocks. Stochastic NPV simulation confirms that SWIFT friction elimination surplus (Δ𝑆 𝑡) fully cross-subsidizes off-grid multi-energy infrastructure (𝐾 𝑖𝑛𝑑), maintaining a strictly positive return (𝔼[𝑁𝑃𝑉] > 0) with near-zero price variance (𝜎 2 → 0). Continuous-time Markov Chain modeling demonstrates that under simultaneous subsea optical fiber cuts and Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite jamming, automated failover to High-Frequency (HF) radio reduces systemic halt probability toward zero (𝑃(𝑆 4) → 0.00%), guaranteeing 𝑃 𝑠𝑢𝑟𝑣𝑖𝑣𝑒 = 100% operational uptime. Finally, game-theoretic consensus modeling proves that subsidizing pooled micro-entity validator nodes (𝑊 𝑝𝑜𝑜𝑙) enforces a strict decentralization inequality (max(𝑊 𝑎𝑐𝑡𝑜𝑟) < 1 3 𝒲 𝑡𝑜𝑡𝑎𝑙), permanently preventing single-actor vetoes or network takeovers. These findings confirm that IICSS Part III grounds monetary sovereignty in robust thermodynamic and physical resilience.

detail.abstract: Households increasingly concentrate their spending on a smaller set of familiar products, which may give firms more power over loyal consumers. Theory suggests that Internet access could hasten this trend: consumers can more easily compare prices for their favorite products, and advertisers can use greater data availability to target ads and coupons. In this paper, I study how smartphone access affects consumers at the grocery store. Using state-level random forests, I construct the first public, national dataset on 3G rollout, a prerequisite for smartphone use. I find that smartphone access shifts purchases toward smaller brands and weakly reduces household spending concentration, as consumers buy more distinct brands and products. Counter to general trends, I find that consumers become more likely to purchase products where they differ from the "typical" consumer. I also find no significant change in posted prices or in-store offerings. Demand estimation shows that smartphones shrink price elasticities but do not generally affect brand relevance. These results run counter to the information mechanisms usually proposed for smartphones' effect on shopping. Instead, I propose in-store distraction as the most likely explanation.

In the face of rapid demographic aging, East Asian economies have developed contrasting long‑term care (LTC) approaches, with Taiwan relying on market‑based migrant caregiving and Japan implementing universal public insurance.
Most existing literature predominantly relies on static cross-sectional comparisons,
leaving less explored the resilience of welfare arrangements and the ways in which macroeconomic shocks reshape intra‑household resource allocation.
Exploiting the 2020 cross-border migrant labor supply disruption as a quasi-natural
experiment, we link a decade of harmonized panel data (2012--2022) from the Panel
Study of Family Dynamics (PSFD) and the Japan Household Panel Survey (JHPS) to examine
the ``Care Crowding-Out Effect'' through Event Study and Difference-in-Differences (DID)
frameworks.

Our empirical analysis yields four primary findings.
First, following the external shock, Taiwanese households experienced a severe financial
price shock, characterized by a significant surge in upward financial transfers, while family
caregiving hours remained relatively stable.
In contrast, Japanese households exhibited a sharp increase in caregiving time without a corresponding surge in financial transfers, illustrating the contrasting rigidities of the two regimes.

Second, mechanism analyses highlight important health-related non-linearities: while cash
support increased among households with parents in good health, it declined sharply
among households with care-dependent parents (–4.37 percentage points in income share),
suggesting a substitution of informal family care time for rationed formal services.
Third, the severe shortage of market-based care did not widen traditional gender
disparities. Instead, adult sons and daughters showed converging financial and
caregiving contributions, suggesting pragmatic intra-household risk pooling rather
than widening gender specialization.
Finally, liquidity constraints in Taiwan appear to offset the psychological returns
of familial support, resulting in lower subjective well-being among male caregivers
relative to their Japanese counterparts.

Our baseline estimates remain robust to individual fixed effects, full unbalanced panel attrition, and unweighted specifications.
These findings highlight the structural vulnerabilities of single-pillar care regimes and offer relevant implications for designing resilient social safety nets that reconcile public insurance security with cross-border labor flexibility.

detail.abstract: A facility allocates complementary resources among users with different input proportions, under the proportionally fair-equivalently weighted Nash, or Leontief-Fisher-allocation. Expanding one resource reallocates the others and need not raise every user's service. We characterize who gains: user i gains from an expansion of resource k exactly when its requirement vector lies in the open halfspace {a : (G-1 a) k > 0}, where G is the equilibrium-weighted second-moment matrix of requirements. If another resource is used by every user, there are both gainers and losers. With two resources the halfspace collapses to a cutoff on the relative requirement, which rises along the capacity path, making every service path weakly single-peaked: a middle user gains from an early expansion and loses from a later one. From three resources on no coordinate or ratio of coordinates orders the gainers, so dominant-resource reasoning does not extend. These inequalities are exact algebraic questions, and we settle their arithmetic. The allocation is rational at every rational capacity pair if and only if there are at most two distinct input proportions; otherwise rational outcomes are dense but arithmetically thin, and a six-type technology has a dense family of capacities whose allocation has Galois group S 5 and no radical form. Exactness is not conditioning: a nonradical allocation can lie within 5 × 10-8 of a rational one.

detail.abstract: Corporate bankruptcy poses a significant threat to economic stability, occurring when an enterprise is unable to meet its debt obligations and requires creditor intervention. This study employs machine learning techniques to predict the likelihood of corporate insolvency based on key financial indicators. To forecast bankruptcy, we evaluated multiple models: Support Vector Machines (SVM), XGBoost, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and Decision Trees. Our empirical results indicate that Random Forest is the most effective predictive technique, achieving a training accuracy of 99.1%. Furthermore, we implemented several deep learning architectures-specifically Deep Neural Networks (DNN), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), and Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN)-for comparative analysis. These deep learning models yielded highly competitive training accuracies of approximately 98%. Ultimately, this research not only improves upon traditional econometric forecasting models but also establishes a robust machine learning framework for predicting financial distress.

detail.abstract: In small open economies, the extent to which exchange rate depreciations reach consumer prices shapes the conduct of monetary policy. This paper studies whether exchange rate pass-through (ERPT) diers across the conditional distribution of prices, using a novel Bayesian structural quantile VAR that delivers quantile-specic pass-through coecients with credible intervals. We apply it to Peru, an ination-targeting and partially dollarized economy, with quarterly data for 1999Q22026Q1. Pass-through is incomplete and falls along the price chain: at the median, the ERPT after 20 quarters is 0.57 for import prices, 0.25 for producer prices and 0.09 for headline CPI. It is higher at upper quantiles for the three price indices; for headline CPI it is 0.086 at the 10th quantile and 0.103 at the 90th. The dierence between these quantiles after 20 quarters is 0.075 for core CPI, signicant at the 1% level, and 0.022 for non-core CPI, which is not signicant. A linear Bayesian VAR with the same specication gives a single pass-through path, which for core CPI lies within the range of the quantile ERPTs and for the other indices at or below its lower end.

detail.abstract: Patent boxes have emerged as a prominent innovation tax incentive. They offer preferential tax rates on qualifying intellectual property income commonly tied to patent protection. I examine whether these regimes induce firms to substitute from trade secrecy toward patenting. Using their staggered adoption across Europe, I document a large and immediate increase in patenting, consistent with firms bringing unpatented inventions into the public patent system. The response varies with prior protection practices, proprietary disclosure costs, and regime design in ways predicted by the substitution mechanism, while real innovation inputs show little contemporaneous response. Confidential survey evidence around Portugal's 2014 adoption provides direct support for the substitution mechanism: secrecy use declines as patent use rises. Consistent with downstream knowledge-diffusion effects, post-adoption productivity gains increase with firms' technological exposure to the expanded patent stock, while industry concentration declines. These findings highlight a disclosure channel through which patent boxes promote knowledge diffusion, a margin that traditional R&D tax credits do not directly target.

detail.abstract: We study how risk aversion affects both the level and the duration of costly experimentation.  The experimentation level is the per-unit-time intensity of information acquisition.  Extending the framework for endogenous experimentation levels of Moscarini and Smith (2001), we allow a decision-maker to choose consumption, the flow of resources devoted to learning, and when to stop learning and act.  In the CARA benchmark, greater risk aversion always lowers the experimentation level, but its effect on duration is nonmonotonic: at low levels it prolongs learning, whereas at sufficiently high levels it can hasten stopping.  The CRRA extension reveals an additional wealth effect.  Experimentation is short at low wealth because information is expensive in utility terms; it is also shorter at high wealth because the action stake is small relative to lifetime resources and evidence is acquired rapidly.  Thus, experimentation duration alone is not an unambiguous measure of risk aversion: its interpretation requires separating the level from the duration of learning and conditioning on wealth.

detail.abstract: Stated-preference studies elicit individual willingness to pay for environmental change, and benefit-cost practice converts it into social value by summing it across households. That sum coincides with social value only under distributional and fiscal assumptions that are seldom made explicit and rarely estimated. We show that the social value of an environmental improvement equals mean willingness to pay multiplied by a single sufficient statistic, the social value ratio. The statistic captures how willingness to pay is distributed across households with different welfare weights while separating that distributional correction from the level of the weights. It can be estimated from standard dichotomous-choice contingent valuation data that record household income, without a parametric demand model, and reported over a specified range of inequality aversion. Applied to the Deepwater Horizon oil-spill study, the framework places the social value of preventing a future spill 9 to 12 percent below the conventional aggregate. When the improvement is delivered through a corrective tax, consistency requires applying the same welfare weights to those who bear the tax and those who receive its revenue. Doing so can reverse the sign of the fiscal component relative to the unit-weight benchmark, because labor-tax cuts accrue mainly to households with below-average welfare weights. The framework identifies what valuation surveys must collect for internally consistent policy appraisal.

detail.abstract: Respiratory diseases represent a major global health problem, and automated auscultation via deep learning offers a promising path for scalable, low-cost screening. However, clinical deployment of such systems faces two fundamental obstacles: (1) patient-level data heterogeneity—where recordings from the same patient are statistically correlated—violates the independent and identically distributed (IID) assumption underlying standard training pipelines; and (2) high-parameter-count neural networks are incompatible with the memory and compute constraints of portable stethoscope hardware. We propose a novel two-stage knowledge distillation framework that explicitly addresses both challenges. In the first stage, a teacher network (BLNet) is pretrained using a chest-location blocking variable to remove patient-specific confusing factors from learned feature representations. BLNet integrates ResNet and GoogLeNet convolutional blocks with self-attention mechanisms to capture multi-scale temporal and spectral patterns in respiratory audio. In the second stage, a lightweight student network is trained via dual-path distillation: an embedding-level L2 loss transfers feature representations from the teacher, while a temperature-scaled Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence loss propagates softened class probability distributions. Here evaluated on the ICBHI-2017 benchmark under a strict patient-level (no patient overlap) data split. With patient-level split, the proposed method achieves an ICBHI Score of 0.72, matching the full teacher network while using only 87% of its parameters. This represents a 14 percentage point improvement over a student trained without distillation. Ablation analysis demonstrates the importance of non-IID-aware teacher pretraining: replacing BLNet with a standard CNN teacher reduces the ICBHI Score by 6 points, confirming that the blocking variable is critical for downstream distillation quality.

detail.abstract: Persistent poor performance in mathematics among Nigerian secondary school students has contributed to increasing reliance on supplementary paid tutoring. While previous studies have examined factors associated with mathematics achievement, little is known about students' willingness to participate in supplementary tutoring when time commitment is considered as a behavioral cost. This study applied a behavioral economics framework to examine secondary school students' willingness to participate in paid mathematics tutoring and to quantify the amount of weekly tutoring time they were willing to commit. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 62 secondary school students in Ibadan, Oyo State, Nigeria. A modified Hypothetical Purchase Task (HPT) was used to assess willingness across 16 hypothetical tutoring durations ranging from 0 to 15 hours per week (P0 to P15), assuming that parents or guardians covered the financial cost of tutoring. Demand curves were generated from the proportion of students willing to participate at each time-cost level. Generalized linear mixed-effects models were used to examine the effects of tutoring duration, gender, and educational level on willingness. Willingness was highest at lower time commitments, with 95.2% of students willing to participate at one hour per week. Demand declined progressively as tutoring duration increased, with willingness at 50% between 7 and 8 hours. The mixed-effects model showed that increasing tutoring duration significantly reduced willingness to participate (β =-0.329, p < .001). Gender was not significantly associated with willingness (p = .308), whereas senior secondary school students demonstrated significantly greater willingness than junior secondary school students (β = 0.83, p = .031). Time commitment is an important behavioral constraint influencing demand for supplementary mathematics tutoring. Behavioral economic approaches, such as the Hypothetical Purchase Task, provide a useful framework for understanding educational decision-making and may help inform the design of tutoring programmes that maximize student participation.

detail.abstract: The Fundamental Doubt & Conceptual Breakthrough: Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) encompass 10 10 to 10 12 parameters trained over trillions of tokens, making full-network retraining or architectural surgery to embed cryptographic provenance watermarks computationally and thermodynamically impossible. A natural engineering intuition is to freeze 100% of the pretrained LLM backbone and attach a lightweight, fixed-weight watermark block at the output head. However, our first-principles mathematical and empirical audit reveals that both naive fixed-weight blocks and state-of-the-art token-level watermarks (Kirchenbauer et al., ICML, 2023; Kuditipudi et al., TMLR, 2024) suffer from four fundamental failure modes: (1) The Intra-Formula Symbolic Corruption Trap, where constant logit shifts (δ = 2.0) or even memoryless entropy gates corrupt deterministic numbers, biomechanical units, and transitional variable tokens inside multi-step partial differential equations (27.1% numerical error and +34.2% perplexity inflation for a naive fixed block; 3.3% intra-formula corruption for memoryless entropy gating); (2) Phase Shattering Under Paraphrase & Indels, where sliding-window n-gram hashes lose synchronization (5.8% true positive rate under a 30% edit attack); (3) Vulnerability to Spoofing/Splicing & Open-Weight Stripping, where adversaries either delete an external wrapper module or splice human-written paragraphs into watermarked documents; and (4) Severe False-Positive Bias Against Non-Native (ESL) Human Writers (85.7% false-positive rate for post-hoc perplexity detectors; Liang et al., Patterns, 2023). Here, we originate from an unexplored biophysical question: why do artificial neural networks treat logit perturbations as memoryless algebraic shifts, whereas living cytoskeletal proteins such as talin and extracellular matrix hydrogels use fractional viscoelastic stress memory and force-gated catch-bonds to protect structural integrity while transmitting mechanical information? We invent the Mechano-Allosteric Catch-Bond & Visco-Elastic Null-Space Phase-Locking Watermark (MAC-VENPW). MAC-VENPW models the frozen LLM's probability simplex as a Fractional Caputo-Zener Viscoelastic Continuum coupled to M = 4 talin-inspired Cryptic Orthogonal Subspace Bundles (R3, R8, R10, R12) embedded inside the zero-sum synonym null-space of the frozen unembedding matrix W U. Across N = 1, 200 passages, MAC-VENPW achieves 100.0% exact numerical and PDE formula fidelity, restricts perplexity drift to +0.80%, sustains 99.33% TPR (Z = 12.73 ± 2.44, p = 3.73 × 10-149) under 30% paraphrase + indel attacks via 4-band Lomb-Scargle spectral demodulation, exhibits 0.0% ESL false-positive rate, localizes spliced human forgery spans via Eshelby's Configurational Stress Tensor (IoU = 0.942), embeds a 64-bit Walsh-Hadamard payload (99.41% bit accuracy), survives student knowledge distillation (Z radioactive = 8.94 at 25% teacher data), and folds algebraically into W U (D KS = 0.0781, p = 0.832) with zero extra inference FLOPs.

detail.abstract: Non-timber forest products (NTFPs) sustain over 500 million forest dwellers across India, contributing 40% to 60% of household incomes. Despite protections under the Forest Rights Act (2006) and the national Minimum Support Price for Minor Forest Produce (MSP for MFP) scheme, primary gatherers face volatile returns and fragmented institutional support. This paper examines how state procurement frameworks, market mechanisms, and community enterprises operate through a comparative empirical study of Assam, West Bengal, and Jharkhand. Drawing on field interviews with state corporations, federations, and Joint Forest Management Committees alongside primary price-margin data, the study reveals critical structural bottlenecks: statutory MSPs disconnected from market realities (evident in Jharkhand, where open-market lac prices reach Rs 700/kg against an MSP of Rs 200/kg); declining public procurement funds in North Bengal (contracting by over 80%); and rigid FSSAI compliance barriers excluding self-help groups. In contrast, the Siladon cluster in Jharkhand-generating Rs 1.4 crore annually through manual, offline operations-demonstrates that grassroots aggregation and processing can succeed when institutional linkages are dependable. The paper argues for market-sensitive pricing, decentralized processing infrastructure, and transparent supply-chain information systems.

detail.abstract: We check performance persistence of US corporate bonds included in closed-end funds in terms of both market price returns and net asset value average returns in each category. In addition, we use regression models to test market timing ability. We use the entire population of 603 closedend funds over the period 01/01/2010 to 01/01/2025. The data was obtained from Financial Investment View database. Positive returns indicate that the manager is skillful in terms of share picking ability. In addition, I am going to test for market timing ability to measure if the fund manager can outperform the market index. The market timing ability is verified using the Treynor-Mazuy (1966) model and denoted by the coefficient . If the coefficient is positive this indicates that the manager has superior timing ability. Based on my regression results, thirteen out of the twenty three sectors display a coefficient of market timing ability  that is positive and statistically significant at 5% level. A positive  indicates skilled fund manager whose decisions add value to the fund. Their ability to outperform the benchmark index is based on skill and not luck. Eighteen out of the twenty three sectors display positive figures for both the share and NAV average returns. Positive returns indicate that the manager is skillful in terms of share picking ability. The findings are interesting to both practitioners and investors in terms of distinguishing luck from skill and to identify the manager who dispose superior market timing ability.

detail.abstract: Background: Field Amputation (FA) is a rare, but potentially life-saving procedure undertaken by helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS) in the UK. detail.abstract:
African universities generate research with considerable potential to address economic, technological and
social challenges. Yet the institutional processes through which research becomes a licensed technology, a
viable enterprise or a widely adopted innovation remain unevenly developed. This paper examines the
relationship between intellectual property management and research commercialisation through a comparative
qualitative study of Makerere University in Uganda, the University of Nairobi in Kenya, the University of
Cape Town and Stellenbosch University in South Africa.
Drawing on institutional intellectual property policies, technology-transfer arrangements, public reports and
documented commercialisation activities, the study compares the four universities across intellectual property
governance, technology validation, financing, licensing, venture creation, industry engagement and
deployment outcomes. It distinguishes the existence of formal commercialisation structures from evidence that
those structures deliver measurable results.
The analysis suggests that intellectual property protection, although essential in appropriate cases, does not by
itself provide a reliable pathway from research to market or societal use. The institutional challenge lies in
connecting rights management with technical validation, market assessment, specialised commercialisation
expertise, suitable financing and sustained relationships with potential users. Differences among the four
universities also indicate the importance of institutional resources, regulatory environments and access to
established innovation networks.
Building on these findings, the paper proposes the African University Research-to-Outcome and Revenue
Architecture (AURORA), a framework for diagnosing weaknesses in university commercialisation systems
and designing more integrated responses. Its principal elements include stage-appropriate financing,
technology-readiness assessment, complementary licensing and venture-creation pathways, shared regional
technology-transfer services and performance measures that recognise both commercial returns and public
benefit. The paper is explicit that revenue is one outcome among several, not the sole measure of research
value.
The paper contributes to debates on African university innovation by shifting attention from the accumulation
of intellectual property rights towards the institutional conditions under which research-generated knowledge
can be deployed. Its findings are analytically grounded in four cases and provide a basis for further comparative
research and institutional testing of the proposed framework.

detail.abstract: Forecasting short-term gold price movements is challenging because gold prices may reflect information from both the gold market and related financial markets. This study investigates whether Bitcoin market information and relative trading activity between Bitcoin and gold provide additional information for one-dayahead gold price direction prediction. We propose cross-market relative activity features that log-transform trading volume, standardize activity within each market using rolling windows, and measure the difference between the standardized activity levels of Bitcoin and COMEX gold futures. The proposed representation is evaluated using three feature settings: gold-derived features, combined gold-and Bitcoin-derived features, and the combined features augmented with the proposed cross-market activity features. Five tree-based ensemble classifiers-Random Forest, Extra Trees, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoostare evaluated using monthly walk-forward validation. Adding Bitcoin-derived features alone does not consistently improve performance, whereas the proposed features increase the aggregate F1-score for all five classifiers. The largest improvements are observed for CatBoost (+0.061), XGBoost (+0.060), and LightGBM (+0.050), with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests indicating significant monthly differences for LightGBM (p=0.027) and CatBoost (p=0.042). These results suggest that explicitly representing relative cross-market trading activity can complement market-specific features, although its effectiveness remains model-dependent.

detail.abstract: Financial inclusion and sustainable entrepreneurial development across Sub-Saharan Africa face an enduring structural dilemma: while regenerative entrepreneurship (notably in smallholder agriculture, agro-processing, local crafts, and ecological transitions) requires patient capital, risk protection, and relational support, prevailing digital credit models prioritize rapid loan turnover and high transaction velocity. Concurrently, although annual remittance inflows exceed $50 billion, diaspora capital remains overwhelmingly channeled into immediate consumption rather than productive enterprise equity due to cross-border information asymmetries and weak monitoring architectures. This paper examines how diaspora finance and Slow Finance microequity offer essential institutional alternatives to debt-driven microcredit, drawing conceptual foundations from Woody Tasch’s Slow Money movement, the seven-point taxonomy of grassroots fiduciary capital (Jayashankar, Ashta, & Rasmussen, 2015), civic solidarity investing (such as the French CIGALES), and transnational diaspora investment literature. Against this backdrop, we analyze how artificial intelligence (AI) and programmable rails can resolve the historical operational bottlenecks of diaspora micro-investing without imposing extractive velocity on local ventures. While initial coin offerings (ICOs) demonstrated that digital tokens can finance firm-level projects, their widespread governance failures highlight the danger of purely speculative, unanchored tokenization. We demonstrate that AI cannot alter the inherently slow, biological pace of sustainable agricultural enterprise; its legitimate developmental value lies in accelerating due diligence, verifying alternative ledgers, and automating cross-border revenue splits. We conclude that by linking digital payment rails to automated revenue-split smart contracts and decentralized oracles, hybrid intelligence can transform transnational remittances into patient, community-anchored equity for unincorporated sustainable enterprises.

detail.abstract: This paper tests whether unconditional cash transfers reduce women's work, using six Indian state programmes launched in 2018-2023: four pay women monthly and two pay farming households. We compare treated states with untreated neighbours in national labour-force microdata, under two pre-period baselines and across synthetic-control, border-district and staggered-adoption estimators. Female participation did not fall under any women's scheme, at minimum detectable effects of one to six points, and coverage of a quarter to four fifths of eligible women carries the null to recipients. Where cash reached farming households in Telangana and Odisha, family farm work intensified: women entered as unpaid family workers and Telangana's men left wage work for own-account cultivation. Assam's women's transfer did the same in its first year. Pooled-baseline exits in West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh are pre-launch trends that vanish against the last pre-launch round. In Karnataka, where cash arrived two months after the Shakti scheme made bus travel free for women and lowered entry barriers to work, contracted regular work among urban women rose five points under the pooled baseline, in jobs women already held, concentrated in Bengaluru. We read the cell as the formal-entry margin opening and print the case against: the rise predates the launch by a year, on a contract item converging across the state's regular workforce. On MGNREGA records, women's share of workfare demand never fell after a transfer, and Karnataka's pre-committed null holds. Cash financed family production where working capital bound and, on our reading of urban Karnataka, formal work where Shakti had lowered the barriers to entry.

detail.abstract: On-demand service platforms offer flexible service options that allow customers to exchange longer waiting times for lower prices. Such waiting flexibility creates an operational challenge: platforms must determine when to fulfill flexible demand and when to reserve capacity for customers requesting immediate service. We study this dynamic service allocation problem in a two-sided on-demand platform that offers a full-priced regular service and a discounted Wait-and-Save (W&S) service. The W&S service features a maximum waiting time guarantee paired with a compensation scheme upon expiration. Customers may renege while waiting due to impatience. We formulate the problem as an infinite-horizon long-run average reward Markov decision process (MDP), which suffers from the curse of dimensionality. We construct a discrete-time fluid approximation and derive an age-dependent, threshold-type heuristic policy that strategically delays fulfilling W&S demand until the customer waiting age reaches a critical threshold. Our analysis reveals a priority reversal structure: service priorities should be determined by supply condition. Specifically, regular customers receive priority when supply is ample, whereas W&S customers whose waiting ages exceed the threshold take priority during supply shortages. We prove that the proposed age-dependent threshold policy is asymptotically optimal, achieving a loss ratio of order O(1/n) as the market scale n grows large. We compare the performance of our age-dependent threshold policy with other heuristics, including a static allocation policy and a state-dependent allocation policy. We further extend the model to a continuous-time setting, showing that the dynamic control problem can be reduced to optimizing the W&S dispatching age threshold.

detail.abstract: A government can reach the same supplies of money and debt by increasing money before debt or in the reverse order. When bond holdings and fiscal burdens differ across households, these implementation methods also affect households differently. Each increase changes the bond prices and fiscal payments through which the other affects households. I examine how far the government can adjust these distributional effects by changing the interval between the increases and debt maturity. Debt management has limited power to undo the effects of policy order for both households. When households without bonds bear part of the fiscal burden, the prices at which debt is issued constrain what maturity adjustments can achieve. Offsetting the effects on both households may require retiring existing short-term debt rather than simply issuing more long-term debt. Thus, the distributional power of debt management depends on who bears the fiscal burden and how much existing debt the government can retire.

detail.abstract: The paper studies software agents built from a 2,000-neuron subgraph of MaleCNS, a reconstructed map of a male fruit fly's neural connections. The agents face Holt-Laury lotteries, the Allais paradox and a repeated Prisoner's Dilemma, with published human experiments providing the benchmarks. They make fewer safe lottery choices than humans-4.125 against 5.2-yet all 24 primary controllers exhibit the conventional Allais reversal. In repeated interaction, cooperation averages approximately 38% and declines with experience. The agents respond to a reciprocal opponent but fail to reproduce humans' high initial cooperation followed by terminal defection in later matches. Control treatments show that changes in neural connections, payoff representation and learning speed affect the agents' choices. Simulated flies thus offer a complementary class of experimental subjects for studying preferences and strategic behavior.

detail.abstract: The diffusion of generative AI across industries raises the question of who is affected by the resulting labour-market adjustment. Using 12.3 million person-months of US Current Population Survey data from 2015 to 2026 and the task-based codifiablesubstitution decomposition of Verschuere and Cameron (2026), we identify two patterns at the subset of US industries that have adopted generative AI (both of which also remain detectable on the full 23-industry panel). First, AI substitutes lower-skilled tasks for every worker regardless of age. Second, at higher-skilled work, age and educational credential shield prime workers (35-49) from substitution exposure while young workers (22-25) at the same positions are not shielded. The age-shielding gradient appears across task position, educational credential, and occupation wage, and, within task tiers, concentrates at occupations with high judgment content. A low-AI industry placebo returns null age differentials, ruling out general 2024-26 employment trends. We show the organizing mechanism is a mediation of Amdahl's Law into labor economics within the job. The complementation share binds as the substitutable share is accelerated.

detail.abstract: Health systems make decisions that depend on the coming weather, such as when to open cooling centers, and each needs warning at a particular lead time. Climate services for health have rarely been built around those decisions. Physics-based forecasting needed hundred-million-dollar supercomputers, took months to rebuild around a new user’s question, and was costly to tailor locally, so services were built around what could be produced. AI weather models remove these constraints. They match or beat leading physics-based forecasts at a fraction of the cost and can be rebuilt in days. We argue that a decision-first approach, in which the owners of a health decision specify what a forecast must do before it is built, is now within reach of any weather service, not only the wealthiest. With forecast quality no longer the main barrier, the rest of the chain from forecast to health outcome becomes worth fixing: decisions nobody specified, forecasts judged on atmospheric accuracy, no record of whether warnings helped, and no one assigned to act on them. Benchmarking - comparing models against each other to evaluate which best could support a particular decision - decides which models get developed next, and current AI weather benchmarks reward performance in data-rich regions. Left to these incentives, AI forecasting may again leave behind the populations the first forecasting revolution never reached. A series of investments to build AI weather forecasting capacity around the needs of the people with the greatest unmet burden. Evaluations of weather warnings have rarely measured health outcomes, so funders should build that evidence before paying to scale. We draw on a literature review, dozens of expert interviews, and a June 2026 convening.

detail.abstract: The relationship between immigration and crime is one of the most salient issues in public discourse. Despite widespread public concern, most studies find no evidence that immigration increases crime rates in host countries. This article reviews recent empirical evidence on the relationship between immigration and crime. Rather than offering an exhaustive survey, it focuses on recent and seminal contributions, highlighting emerging trends and research frontiers. In particular, the article discusses how immigration policies can mediate the relationship between immigration and crime. It also discusses research on crimes against immigrants, a topic that has attracted increasing scholarly interest but remains largely neglected in public discourse. Finally, given the substantial gap between public perception and the empirical evidence, the article reviews research on immigration and crime perception.

detail.abstract: The fiscal institutions proposed against long-term deficits-balanced-budget rules, tax and expenditure limits, supermajority requirements-share a grammar: they are rules about totals, written on the government, and their drafting presumes the two things classical political economy warns against presuming: knowledge the rule-writer does not possess and virtue the rule-enforcer need not have. We read Personal Tax Holding (PTH)-a constitutional generalization of the percentage-philanthropy statutes of Central and Eastern Europe, under which every citizen annually directs a fixed fraction of her own tax liability to certified public-goods organizations, undirected accounts expiring to the treasury-through the Austrian tradition: Mises's calculation problem, Hayek's knowledge problem and competition as a discovery procedure, and the robust-political-economy standard that institutions be judged under worst-case assumptions about both knowledge and motivation. So read, the mechanism's formal properties acquire their proper names. The designated margin is pay-as-you-go by an accounting identity-the old-time fiscal religion restored on a constitutional slice, with nothing assigned to anyone to enforce. Aggregate lapsing is the only demand statistic an involuntary fiscal system produces-demonstrated preference in the negative-and the friction-adjusted levy rule that reads it is epistemic humility written into law. The ceiling-enforcing coalition of never-designating citizens is a spontaneous order, of human action but not of human design, whose blocking power rests on the government's ignorance of who designated: the knowledge problem turned to the constitution's advantage. Certification by margin caps delegates quality to competition as discovery. An Austrian audit records the limits: designation is choice within compulsion, its signals are quantities rather than prices, and formal robustness parametrizes an ignorance it cannot fully honor.

detail.abstract:
This study examines the relationship between international trade and economic growth in Pakistan over the period 2003–2018. It investigates the role of trade volume, export diversification, and gross fixed capital formation in explaining economic growth. The study uses secondary data from the World Bank and employs regression analysis to examine the relationships among these variables.

The reported results indicate a negative relationship between trade volume and economic growth, while export diversification and gross fixed capital formation have positive estimated coefficients. The regression model reports an R-squared value of 0.532, indicating that the included explanatory variables account for 53.2% of the variation in the dependent variable in the reported estimation. The study also reports an overall model significance level of 0.02. However, the findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited sample period, potential omitted variables, and limitations of the regression model.

The study highlights the importance of carefully designed trade policies, export diversification, and investment in infrastructure and technology. It recommends further research using a larger dataset and additional economic variables to develop a more comprehensive understanding of the relationship between international trade and economic growth in Pakistan.

detail.abstract: On weakly governed frontiers, land is often illegally occupied. This paper asks whether securing land against this process can reduce modern slavery. We study the Brazilian Amazon, where the activities that occupy this land rely on geographically isolated workers with few options outside the region. We argue that these activities can sustain demand for vulnerable workers who are kept in slavery conditions. By removing land from the set of areas available for private appropriation, formal protection can weaken this coercive frontier economy. To test this hypothesis, we exploit the staggered expansion of Indigenous lands and ecological protected areas across municipalities of the Legal Amazon from 1997 to 2019. The empirical strategy combines the timing of protected-area expansion with federal slave-labor inspection records and individual-level data on rescued workers. Consistent with the hypothesis, we find that protection strongly reduces the probability that an inspection finds slavery and the number of workers released in affected municipalities. This reduction is concentrated primarily in cattle ranching, the sector most directly linked to land grabbing in the Amazon due to its low implementation cost. Additionally, protection displaces part of this activity to nearby municipalities where land can still be claimed.

detail.abstract: Decentralization is meant to make governments more accountable to voters, but when local officials depend on discretionary central transfers, it can instead make them accountable to the center. We formalize this idea in a probabilistic voting model of two-layered clientelism. A central government allocates workfare across municipalities and chooses whether programs are administered by local mayors or by state-owned enterprises. Because mayors value control over these jobs, the center can discipline them by conditioning future funding on municipalities' support for the governing party in national elections, turning them into vote brokers. Using municipality-level administrative data on Hungary's workfare program and a difference-indifferences design, we find that workfare raised support for both the national incumbent and local mayors, with the estimates concentrated in mayor-managed programs. Municipalities that delivered weaker national support subsequently lost mayor-managed positions, even under incumbent-aligned mayors: the center punished electoral underperformance, not partisan misalignment. Discretionary local control and politically contingent funding can thus turn a decentralized welfare program into an instrument of clientelism.

detail.abstract: Carbon lock-in is the puzzle of why fossil fuel technologies endure long after cleaner ones become available. The concept, due to Unruh (2000), has been widely adopted but thinly formalized. Existing accounts are mostly qualitative or reduced-form, and the rare formal treatments recast the problem in growth-theoretic terms, leaving aside Unruh's own mechanism, the pull between increasing returns and barriers to adoption. This paper develops a parsimonious dynamic model in which supply-side increasing returns to scale, demand-side increasing returns to adoption, and the population distribution of consumer preferences jointly determine the equilibrium structure of competition between a carbon-based incumbent technology and a green challenger. Three results emerge. First, under constant returns on both sides of the market the equilibrium is unique for any preference distribution, so lock-in cannot arise. Second, under moderate increasing returns the system admits multiple equilibria only when preferences are approximately neutral between technologies, which identifies preference formation as a decisive margin for climate policy. Third, and most consequentially, when increasing returns are strong the market share locus becomes so flat that every admissible preference distribution intersects it three times. Multiplicity then becomes a structural property of the market that no campaign to reshape preferences can remove on its own. In that regime history alone selects the equilibrium, temporary interventions dissipate unless they push adoption past an interior tipping threshold, and the economy can remain trapped in a high-emission equilibrium that a majority of consumers privately disprefer. The analysis delivers a sharp policy taxonomy. Preference-side instruments are sufficient only under weak increasing returns, whereas strong increasing returns require coordinated, threshold-crossing interventions on both the price gap and the adoption externality.

detail.abstract:
Identifying the natural person who ultimately owns or controls an asset—known as the beneficial owner—is a key transparency measure to prevent misuse for criminal or unethical purposes. This is especially critical in high-risk sectors, where vulnerabilities are amplified during economic or existential crises, such as financial bubbles or climate change. While many countries are establishing centralized beneficial ownership registries—often linked to commercial registers for anti-money laundering/combating the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) compliance—these may not fully meet the needs of sector-specific oversight. Agencies like procurement authorities or land registries often require more granular or tailored beneficial ownership data, such as information on foreign entities or lower thresholds for politically exposed persons (PEPs). 

A sectoral approach to beneficial ownership transparency addresses these gaps by aligning data collection and use with the unique risks and operational realities of each sector. This allows for flexible implementation—from basic disclosures in transactions to advanced verification—while complementing national beneficial ownership frameworks. Importantly, the design should consider sectoral capacity and minimize compliance burdens. Drawing on lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic, where beneficial ownership transparency in procurement helped mitigate corruption risks, this approach is now being explored for other high-risk areas such as real estate, which is particularly vulnerable to money laundering.

detail.abstract: This paper evaluates the effects of the European Union’s (EU) regional trade agreements (RTAs) on trade patterns, with a particular focus on diversification. Using a structural gravity model with data for 170 industries, we exploit variation in RTA depth, measured by the number of legally enforceable provisions, to estimate the effects of deep trade agreements, allowing for heterogeneity across sectors. We then use these estimates to evaluate recent and prospective EU agreements, including EU–Mercosur and EU–India, by analyzing their legal texts and constructing novel measures of agreement depth. The results show that deeper RTAs significantly increase bilateral trade, with substantial sectoral heterogeneity, and promote diversification across products and trading partners. Counterfactual general equilibrium simulations indicate that new agreements further strengthen diversification by reducing import concentration, including in green and strategic sectors, thereby enhancing supply chain resilience.

detail.abstract: Few institutional changes in the developing world have matched the scale and consequence of China's rural land reforms, which since 1978 have progressively expanded farmers' rights from contracted rights to contracted and transferable management rights. This article reviews the economic evidence, organizing the reform trajectory into three stages: decollectivization, tenure strengthening, and land transferability under the Three Rights Separation institution (ownership, contracting rights, and management rights). We find that tenure security generates modest investment responses, while allocative efficiency gains from land transfer and rental markets and labor reallocation are quantitatively large. Transaction costs, endowment effects, and implementation gaps remain significant frictions. The evidence points to heterogeneity by crop type: staple grains require scale economies through consolidation, while high-value crops may follow a small-scale path. Socialized agricultural services offer a complementary channel whose net effects vary by region. We discuss implications for the regionally differentiated pace of farm consolidation.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a stress test framework for nonfinancial corporate (NFC) balance sheets. The model simulates firm income statements and balance sheets conditional on macro-financial scenarios, to obtain conventional risk metrics such as probabilities of default (PDs) and loss given default (LGD), alongside other structural metrics such as interest coverage ratios, leverage, and others. The model entails explicit stock–flow accounting and a link of borrowing costs to firm-specific credit risk metrics, i.e., an endogenous cost of funding feedback. An illustration is provided with an application to Brazil, involving 8,000 private firms and three hundred listed nonfinancial firms. The results point to heightened vulnerabilities under stagflation shock scenarios, which jointly weaken earnings and raise funding costs, increasing default risk and debt at risk.

detail.abstract: Purpose: This paper examines how locus of control relates to body mass among adults aged 50 and over in Europe, and whether the relation differs by gender and by the cultural individualism of countries. Design/methodology/approach: Using seven waves of the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (2006 to 2022) for 10 countries, covering 95,086 person-wave observations on 45,677 individuals, we estimate individual fixed-effects models of body mass index (BMI) on an 11-item locus-of-control index, with heterogeneity by gender and by revised individualism scores. Findings: A more internal locus of control is associated with higher, not lower, BMI. The association is statistically significant but small: a one-standard-deviation increase in the index corresponds to 0.07 BMI points, about 0.2 kg. It holds for men and women and in more and less individualistic countries, with no significant differences across groups. Research limitations/implications: BMI is self-reported, and the within-person association may reflect health shocks that lower both perceived control and body weight. Practical implications: Programs that strengthen perceived control are unlikely to reduce body weight in later life. Social implications: In ageing societies, obesity policy for older adults should not rely on personal-agency interventions, whatever the cultural context. Originality/value: This is the first crosscountry panel evidence on locus of control and body mass in later life, and the first test of cultural moderation using revised individualism measures.

detail.abstract: Do economics papers that report statistically insignificant main results have to be better written in order to be published? Experimental evidence shows that researchers judge studies with null results as less publishable than otherwise identical studies with significant results. If this penalty operates in peer review, null-result papers that are eventually published should compensate on other dimensions, including the clarity of their writing. I test this prediction using articles published in the American Economic Review, the Journal of Political Economy and the Quarterly Journal of Economics between 2015 and 2025. For each article, I code whether the abstract and the introduction report a statistically significant main result, and I measure writing quality with standard readability formulas. To avoid a mechanical link between the result and the score, readability is computed on the parts of the text that do not report results. To separate selection from the effect of peer review, I compare published articles with their working-paper drafts. Once the sentences that state results are set aside, abstracts and introductions reporting at least one non-significant result are as readable as those reporting only significant results, both in the working-paper and in the published version, and the difference observed in the readability of whole abstracts stems entirely from the wording of the results themselves. During the review process, non-significant results tend to disappear from abstracts but not from introductions.

detail.abstract: This paper constructs a country-level panel of estimated international stablecoin flows, covering 188 countries, totaling $21.4 trillion in gross flows between 2018 and 2025. Activity is disproportionately concentrated in emerging markets and developing economies, which hold three quarters of stablecoins. When countries restrict capital outflows, stablecoin activity rises by roughly 30 percent over the following six months, then plateaus, and does not fall back when restrictions are removed. When currency crises hit, stablecoin holdings increase by roughly 75 percent within a year, and the new holdings persist. Both findings suggest that dollarization may now also operate through stablecoins.

detail.abstract: Capacity Aggregation removes aircraft identities from the planning model, which is convenient but can admit a fleet-level plan that no individual aircraft can execute. We study the decision consequence: the readiness-cost multiplier at which an active drone design first outperforms ground-only service. The pooled Scalar threshold is certified only when a threshold-optimal pooled design can attain the same daily cost under aircraft-specific limits and the common road-shift constraints. The annual 17-village case certifies structurally because its threshold design uses one aircraft. Among 72 controlled six-village instances, 42 certify and 30 require exact individual recourse. A separate 48-case eight-village extension adds 11 positive-benefit multi-aircraft certifications and 20 packing failures. Screening sharply reduces an assignment-check proxy, but not runtime in these small instances. Public operating reports anchor scale only. Certification applies to the stated Scalar threshold, not to the full cost frontier or operator profitability.

detail.abstract: How do financial conditions shape U.S. macroeconomic tail risk, and what is their incremental forecasting value beyond standard macroeconomic predictors? Using quarterly U.S. data from 1971Q1 to 2026Q1, this paper compares macro-only and macro-financial Bayesian VARs. First-lag financial-conditions coefficients are negative for GDP growth and positive for unemployment, with 95% posterior credible intervals excluding zero; second-lag coefficients have opposite signs. Adding financial conditions to the Gaussian VAR raises predicted probabilities of negative GDP growth by 1.5 and 2.5 percentage points at four-and eight-quarter horizons and lowers GDP tail quantiles. However, out-of-sample tests do not establish a general forecast-accuracy improvement. Student-t forecast innovations, simulated with the same Gaussian posterior parameter draws, produce heavier predictive tails. Their positive GDP log-score differences reverse when 2020Q1-2021Q4 forecast targets are excluded, while CRPS favors Gaussian innovations in several comparisons. Financial conditions change measured tail risk without consistently improving forecast accuracy.

detail.abstract: We investigate the determinants of preferences for redistribution across Africa using, for the first time, two waves of the Afrobarometer survey fielded between 2011-2021. The data is nationally representative, covering 36 countries and over 90,000 respondents in total. Our analysis includes a rich set of individual determinants (socioeconomic status, beliefs), allowing for comparisons with results from the prior literature. In addition, we assess how the COVID-19 outbreak relates to these preferences in two ways: i) analysing information from a specialised module on individuals' experience in round 8 in a cross-sectional setting and ii) exploiting the March suspension of the Round 8 fieldwork as a natural experiment to compare countries surveyed before and after the pandemic reached them using a differencein-differences (DiD) approach. We find that support for redistribution falls with age and rises with education. Contrary to standard self-interest models, it also rises with wealth. Institutional attitudes are also important with tax morale being the largest single correlate, followed by institutional trust while perceived corruption enters negatively. Turning to the COVID-19 results, we find that income loss due to the pandemic is significantly associated with lower support for redistribution, while household illness is not. The aggregate DiD estimate points to a decline but it is not statistically significant. We find larger and significant declines among respondents with no formal education and those living in rural areas.

detail.abstract: A renewable energy project can advance through development without securing a financing package that can fund construction. This paper develops a practitioner framework for examining that gap in US utility-scale renewable project finance, with particular attention to solar and battery storage. It organizes financing readiness around five closing gates: credit qualification, independent engineering, tax credit qualification, collateral and coverage, and closing mechanics. Public interconnection data establish substantial attrition but do not identify its financing causes. The framework therefore proposes mechanisms that warrant investigation rather than estimating how much withdrawal they explain. The analysis considers how tax eligibility, construction timing, and documentation affect financing under the 2025 amendments to federal clean electricity credits. Four hypothetical scenarios illustrate interactions among the gates. The central proposition is that earlier reconciliation of commercial, technical, tax, and funding assumptions may prevent some avoidable delays and financing shortfalls. Whether those improvements materially increase project completion requires transaction-level evidence.

detail.abstract: Why do managerial styles persist even when managers turn over? Using personnel records from a large Japanese manufacturer, we estimate manager fixed effects on subordinates' overtime hours as a measure of managerial style. Before promotion, some managers worked under supervisors who demanded more overtime from their subordinates. These managers later tend to demand more overtime from their own subordinates, and our evidence supports the interpretation that managers learn styles from former supervisors. Moreover, the firm repeatedly assigns managers with similar styles to the same sections, sustaining section-level persistence. Together, these processes reproduce managerial styles within an internal labor market.
