detail.abstract:
This paper extends the scalarised lexicographic utility framework of [18] to the case where each consumption tier contains multiple goods. The multi-good case allows each tier to possess its own internal price vector and within-tier substitution pattern. We provide an axiomatic foundation for multi-good lexicographic preferences in the tradition of [9], derive the resulting demand correspondence and its Slutsky structure, and establish empirical restrictions that generalise those of the scalarised benchmark.

The framework specialises to the four-tier convention of the companion paper [18]—Necessities (N), Conveniences (H), Refinements (T), and Money (M)—when the number of tiers is K = 4; the general setup allows K tiers, of which K′ ≤ K are satiable. The money tier is non-satiating and linear. Throughout the equilibrium analysis we keep money as a regular good and work on the full price simplex q ∈ Δ^(D−1); after existence is established, we normalise q_M = 1 and pass to reduced prices p = q^sat / q_M. Each consumption tier may contain multiple goods, so that x_t ∈ R^(d_t) with d_t ≥ 1. The compensated Slutsky matrix is block diagonal with d_t × d_t symmetric, negative semidefinite within-tier blocks; the uncompensated Jacobian is block lower-triangular with rank-one off-diagonal blocks.

We prove existence of a mixed competitive equilibrium for discrete-tier exchange economies on the full price simplex, with money treated as a regular good (Theorem 4.13), under the additional hypothesis that the aggregate satiable bliss is component-wise dominated by the aggregate satiable endowment (hypothesis 4.3); under a stronger but verifiable—and deliberately only conservative—satiable-dominance condition: the satiable endowment strictly exceeds, coordinate-wise, every satiable bundle in the choice set. Under this condition, all satiable goods are in excess supply at equilibrium and their prices are zero; UHC nevertheless holds on the entire interior simplex (Proposition 4.10) and the mixed equilibrium exists unconditionally (Corollary 4.12). The existence theorem is conditional on an upper hemi-continuity (UHC) hypothesis on the full excess demand correspondence. We show that, for each fixed endowment profile, UHC can fail only on a Lebesgue-measure-zero set of prices (Theorem 4.16); this does not imply that UHC holds on the entire simplex for generic endowments, and unconditional existence for generic endowments remains open. We also establish pure-strategy existence (with free disposal and exact clearing) for the class of economies with strictly concave tier aggregators on continuous commodity spaces (Theorem 4.19). The general continuous-goods case without strict concavity remains open (Conjecture 4.24).

We provide a finite-sample identification strategy using a lexicographic maximum likelihood approach derived from a coherent random-utility model with extreme value errors, which avoids the perfect-separation problem through an explicit tie term. We prove consistency and asymptotic normality of the resulting estimator under standard regularity conditions (Theorems 5.10–5.11). We specify a Monte Carlo design across three sample sizes (N = 200, 500, 1000) for assessing the finite-sample performance of the estimator and comparing it with alternative estimator; the design is stated in full so that it can be implemented, and numerical execution is left to future work.

The paper fills the gap left by the scalarised benchmark for discrete-tier economies and identifies the additional obstacles that must be overcome for continuous goods; a complete equilibrium theory for continuous lexicographic economies remains open.

detail.abstract: Between November 2024 and April 2025 the price of gold for delivery on COMEX in New York exceeded the London benchmark price by a margin several times its historical size, and more than ten million troy ounces entered COMEX registered warehouses. The prevailing interpretation attributes the premium to the anticipated extension of United States import tariffs to bullion. This paper tests the event-study implication of that interpretation: if the premium priced tariff risk, it should have widened on news that raised the probability of a bullion tariff and narrowed on news that lowered it. The futures leg is constructed from CME Group daily settlements by explicit contract month with a documented roll rule, and the premium is financed to the delivery month of the contract held. The data comprise 917 trading days from January 2023 to September 2026, eleven tariff event windows dated from the Federal Register and the press, weekly CFTC positioning data, and partial COMEX depository stock records. The financing-adjusted gold premium averaged 0.02 percent of spot over the 2023 to October 2024 baseline (standard deviation 0.70), averaged 0.12 percent from November 2024 to April 2025, reached 1.71 percent (56 dollars an ounce at a London price of 3,279 dollars) on 28 April 2025, and reached 2.27 percent on 2 September 2025 after press reports of a customs ruling. The event study does not detect a response of the premium to general trade-policy news. Over the ten event windows with an unambiguous sign, the mean signed two-day change in the gold premium is minus 0.16 percent (standard error 0.35, t equal to minus 0.44) and 5 of ten events move in the hypothesized direction; the silver mean is 0.23 percent (t equal to 0.36). The seven events that concerned trade policy in general have means of minus 0.50 percent for gold (standard error 0.42) and minus 0.32 for silver (0.78). The three events that concerned bullion specifically have means in the hypothesized direction, 0.64 percent for gold (standard error 0.64, t equal to 0.99, 2 of 3 with the hypothesized sign) and 1.53 for silver (1.19, t equal to 1.29, 3 of 3), driven by the minus 2.14 percent two-day narrowing of the gold premium after the 5 September 2025 exemption order; this evidence is more consistent with the tariff hypothesis than the general events are, but it rests on three events in one episode and does not reject zero. In a regression of the daily premium change on the signed event dummy and financing controls over 372 trading days, the event coefficient is minus 0.08 percent for gold (standard error 0.27) and 0.14 for silver (0.26); adding the same-day futures return moves the gold coefficient to 0.11 (0.22). The placebo on platinum and copper futures returns is an inappropriate test of a location-spread hypothesis, and the absence of a platinum premium series is a limitation of the paper. The results are unchanged under a maturity-matched financing rate and under three roll rules. The paper then asks whether the public record on dealer positioning and warehouse stocks is consistent with an alternative in which the premium compensates dealers for balance-sheet capacity, following Hanson, Malkhozov and Venter (2024) and Greenwood, Hanson, Stein and Sunderam (2023). The evidence for that alternative is weak for gold, where weekly swap-dealer net positions are correlated with the premium at minus 0.32 over 79 weeks, and the model fails for silver: the swap-dealer correlation has the opposite sign (0.25), and the producer and merchant category, which carries the predicted sign (minus 0.30), is not a category that any institutional source links to bullion-bank location books. The primary contribution is the finding, subject to the low power of ten signed events, that general trade-policy news had no detectable effect on the premium at the two-day and ten-day horizons; the limited bullion-specific evidence points in the direction the tariff hypothesis predicts, and the dealer-capacity account is a tentative alternative that the data do not establish for gold and contradict for silver.

detail.abstract: This is an Opinion Statement prepared by the CFE ECJ Task Force on the NOVA IBEROMOLDES – SGPS, S.A. v Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (hereinafter: the "Nova Iberomoldes Case"), in which the Court of Justice of the EU (First Chamber) delivered its decision on 4 June 2026. The judgment clarifies the scope of Directive 2008/7/EC concerning indirect taxes on the raising of capital, in particular, in what concerns the dialectic relationship between the prohibition laid down in Article 5 (of charging any form of indirect tax whatsoever on certain transactions, including restructuring operations) and the derogations set forth in Article 6 of the Directive (namely the possibility of levying taxes on real estate transfers). The Court held that the Directive precluded national real estate transfer tax legislation under which the formation of a capital company, whose share capital is paid up by means of shares held in other companies owning immovable property, is subject to a tax assessed on the indirect transfer of immovable property by reference to the value of that property. The Court did not follow the Opinion of Advocate General Kokott, who had proposed that the Portuguese tax should not be regarded as a prohibited indirect tax on the raising of capital within the meaning of the Directive, since an indirect change of ownership in immovable property by means of a majority shareholding should fall within the exception laid down in Article 6 of the Directive. The judgment raises issues that go far beyond the Portuguese tax system. It holds that where a transfer of shares is itself a contribution of capital or a restructuring operation under Directive 2008/7/EC, the characterisation of a levy on that transfer is determined under EU Law, and it is not altered by a national provision treating the transfer as a transfer of the underlying immovable property. It applies the settled principle that the exceptions in Article 6 are exhaustive and must be interpreted strictly. It also addresses the role of anti-abuse considerations under the Directive, holding that Member States may prevent fraudulent or abusive practices but may not rely on general presumptions of abuse. In essence, the judgment does not prevent Member States from taxing share deals in real-estate owning companies as such. It prevents them from applying such a charge to contributions of capital and restructuring operations that the Directive exempts from any form of indirect tax, unless the particular transaction is shown to be abusive. This Opinion Statement seeks to explain and analyse the CJEU's reasoning in the Nova Iberomoldes case, particularly with respect to its impact on the design of domestic real estate transfer tax systems that assimilate share-deals involving underlying immovable property to such transfers of immovable property.

detail.abstract: Ports increasingly compete on the performance of their hinterland connections, where inland waterway transport (IWT) can provide high-capacity, lower-emission container flows but faces commercial uncertainty driven by volatile demand and shared asset constraints. This paper studies weekly pricing for an anonymized industry-proposed “fast barge” service serving five inland corridors on the Mississippi River system. We formulate a finite-horizon Markov decision process with stochastic, price-sensitive demand, corridor limits, and a shared fleet-hours allocation problem. Shipment manifests calibrate seasonality but contain no transaction prices, so reference tariffs and elasticities are explicit modeling assumptions. We compare transparent tariff, myopic, one-period, and shadow-price policies with proximal policy optimization (PPO), advantage actor–critic (A2C), and soft actor–critic (SAC), using common continuous actions, ten training seeds, and 200 paired evaluation seeds. A loose reference case remains price-boundary driven. A prespecified 300-hour benchmark has an interior unconstrained price and a positive deterministic capacity dual in 48.1% of weeks. In final evaluation, PPO and SAC improve on the validation-selected transparent benchmark by 0.089% (USD 51,800/year) and 0.362% (USD 211,100/year), respectively, with positive hierarchical intervals. Neither meets the prespecified 0.5% primary adoption screen, and the transparent benchmark retains 99.6% of SAC’s mean profit. The economic case for RL is therefore conditional on whether its annualized implementation and governance costs fall below the measured incremental value, rather than supporting an unconditional replacement recommendation.

detail.abstract: Interactive intelligent systems constructed over hosted large language models cannot retrain the substrate on which they depend, and so their designers enforce a named epistemology at the surrounding scaffold layer. A difficulty follows that has received little methodological attention: when quality regresses, the regression frequently belongs to the scaffold rather than the substrate, and identifying it requires instruments that measure the scaffold itself rather than the model beneath it. This article reports one such instrument set, added to a live constitutional runtime between 17 and 18 July 2026 and extended with a production drift observer on 19 August 2026, and situates it as a reusable design pattern. The layer comprises six components—operator-authored adversarial batteries held as versioned regression fixtures, deterministic pattern screens encoding named defects, an emission quarantine that retains failure evidence as a first-class object, an instrument-health monitor issuing autonomous handoffs, continuous-integration delivery tripwires, and an observe-only production drift detector that accumulates a hand-labelling corpus from live traffic without altering any replies. Eight falsifiable harness predictions are stated (H1 through H8), each named against a specific runtime carrier—a code path, a database table, or a typed field—and each paired with an explicit falsification condition; their relationship to the eight pre-registered outcome predictions (F1 through F8) of a companion architecture paper is stated in a dedicated reconciliation section, since the harness reported here is the instrument set on which those outcome predictions depend. Of the eight, five (H1, H2, H3, H5, H7) carry dated on-platform observations and are reported in a dedicated observed subsection; three (H4, H6, H8) are prospective—predictions about experiments that have not yet occurred—and are reported separately under that label, so that no reader mistakes the distribution of evidence. The predictions are offered for adversarial replication under an honest empirical frame rather than as settled results: the batteries were authored by the platform’s operator, classification is not independent, and the number of platforms studied is one. The discussion states a narrow priority claim, distinguishes the enforcement point of composition-time assertion from adjacent techniques, extends the pattern to the governance of learning loops—a scaffold that adapts must be measured by the same discipline that measures a scaffold that enforces—and argues that the interaction properties a reader encounters, an observation lock and per-turn provenance grounding, become testable precisely because they are structurally enforced.

detail.abstract: Timely orthopaedic trauma care in low- and middle-income countries depends not only on infrastructure, but also on how limited operating-theatre capacity is allocated. Routine theatre data may provide practical measures of demand, delay and workload. This study described emergency orthopaedic theatre utilisation in a South African public-sector tertiary hospital.A single-centre retrospective descriptive study used routinely collected emergency-theatre data from 1 January to 31 December 2025. The unit of analysis was the booking episode; episodes were additionally linked by hospital folder number for a patient-level sensitivity analysis. Completed operative episodes were analysed for booking-to-anaesthetic time, operative duration, procedure mix, anatomical distribution and out-of-hours activity under the registry completion-time classification and a staffing-based classification using operation start time, weekday and public holidays. Analyses were descriptive, with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for key proportions.Median booking-to-anaesthetic time among 488 completed operative episodes was 1.38 days (IQR 0.54-2.74); 188 (38.5%, 95% CI 34.3-42.9) proceeded within 24 hours and 102 (20.9%) waited three days or longer. Under the registry classification, 205 episodes (42.0%) were after hours; under the staffing-based classification, 263 (53.9%, 95% CI 49.5-58.3) began out of hours, and 52.3% of the 778 operative hours occurred out of hours, equivalent to 7.8 out-of-hours operative and 12.4 out-of-hours anaesthetic hours per week. Median operative duration was 85 minutes (IQR 45-120; n=487). Washout/debridement (36.8%) and intramedullary nailing (25.7%) dominated the procedure mix; femur and tibia represented 40.5% of operated regions. Of 1,094 booking episodes, 488 (44.6%, 95% CI 41.7-47.6) were completed through the emergency-theatre pathway during the index episode; in local practice, most of the remainder were transferred to and completed on scheduled daytime trauma or elective lists not captured by the registry. At patient level, 422 of 901 linked patients (46.8%) had at least one completed episode. Recategorisation was recorded in 31.6% of bookings.Routine booking data revealed prolonged delay after booking, a majority out-of-hours operative workload and a procedure mix dominated by debridement and long-bone fixation. These measures can inform theatre allocation, implant procurement and staffing, and support prospective evaluation of demand-matched protected daytime trauma capacity in resource-constrained systems.

detail.abstract:
Background: To evaluate changes in emergency department (ED) utilization, presenting triage acuity, in-hospital mortality, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and ED length of stay (LOS) following the 2024 resident physician workforce disruption.

Methods: We used National Emergency Department Information System data for 2023–2024, with February 19, 2024, as the intervention date. Weekly ED visits were analyzed using seasonality-adjusted interrupted time-series negative binomial regression. Clinical outcomes were analyzed using patient-level interrupted time-series generalized linear models, with sequential adjustment for patient and ED characteristics, then Korean Triage and Acuity Scale (KTAS) level.

Findings: We analyzed 15,265,191 ED visits. Weekly ED visits decreased immediately by 24% (incidence rate ratio 0·76, 95% CI 0·68–0·85) and remained below the counterfactual trend. Post-resignation patients were older and more often classified as KTAS 1–3 (54·8% vs 46·2%). Crude in-hospital mortality rose from 1·4% to 1·7%. In patient-level models, the odds ratio (OR) before covariate adjustment was 1·17 (95% CI 1·15–1·19), decreasing to 1·13 (1·11–1·15) after adjustment for patient and ED characteristics and to 1·03 (1·01–1·05) after further KTAS adjustment. After full adjustment, ICU admission odds remained higher (OR 1·14, 1·13–1·15), whereas ED LOS was 11·4% shorter (mean ratio 0·886, 0·885–0·888).​

Interpretation: Among patients presenting to EDs, the workforce disruption was followed by substantially lower ED utilization and a shift toward greater triage acuity. The adjusted association with in-hospital mortality was small, while higher odds of ICU admission and shorter ED LOS remained.

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing marketing from a periodic, campaign-centred activity into a continuous process of sensing, predicting and responding to individual customers. This paper synthesises the academic and industry literature on AI in marketing and organises it around three questions: which AI capabilities matter most, what value they create, and what risks they introduce. Beyond the literature review, the study presents a controlled, synthetic-data experiment that compares four customer-churn targeting approaches (a simple rule, logistic regression, random forest and gradient boosting) and translates their performance into campaign economics. The illustration shows that most of the gain comes from using any risk-based targeting at all, while advanced models add a smaller, though still commercially meaningful, increment over a well-chosen heuristic. The paper then examines privacy, algorithmic bias, opacity, manipulation and skill gaps, compares the GDPR, India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, the EU AI Act and California's CCPA/CPRA, and proposes a five-stage maturity model and a phased implementation roadmap. The paper concludes that sustainable advantage comes not from algorithms alone but from the combination of high-quality first-party data, explainable models, human creative judgement and demonstrable respect for customer autonomy.

detail.abstract: Job seekers increasingly encounter employer information through large language models (LLMs), yet little is known about the portrayals these systems generate. We audit AI-generated employer portrayals using 915,000 controlled prompt-response observations spanning 100 U.S. companies and 61 open-weight models (0.5B-120B parameters), benchmarked against 1.2 million Glassdoor reviews. We find a pattern we call calibration with compression. On average, the models moderately agree with Glassdoor about which companies are better places to work, but they compress the differences between companies. The LLMs' portrayals pull poorly rated employers toward the middle. When portrayals are pooled across models, the spread between companies is only 62% of that in Glassdoor reviews, compared with 85% for the typical individual model. The models also rate career opportunities 0.22 stars higher than the real reviews from 2020 to 2026. Larger models give more stable answers and match real employee reviews more closely (correlation rises from .20 for models of 3B parameters or fewer to .47 for models between 20B and 70B), but large models also tend to agree with one another (r = .80 above 20B). This means that consulting another large model often provides less independent evidence than job seekers may assume. How a model is prompted also matters: asking the model to act as a "neutral" assistant instead of a "helpful" one lowers ratings of companies. Taken together, these results suggest that while AI tools can help job seekers get oriented to the information environment around employers (such as by functioning as a type of search engine), they do not function as a truly independent source of information or as a purely faithful proxy for widely accepted social information sources (like Glassdoor), because they can sound well calibrated while hiding differences that may matter most.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether the effects of class size reduction in early primary grades persist through entry to middle school. I exploit France's national reform, launched in 2017, which halved grade 1 and grade 2 class sizes in disadvantaged schools and produced positive and significant effects on French and mathematics achievement by the end of second grade. Using administrative data spanning nine cohorts of students entering sixth grade from 2017 to 2025, I employ an event study design comparing the evolution of sixth-grade outcomes between students exposed to smaller classes in early grades and those who were not. I find no effect on French, but a positive effect on mathematics, particularly in the most disadvantaged schools. In these schools, the effect increases across successive treated cohorts, reaching 0.078 standard deviations for the fourth cohort. This gain closes approximately 12% of the pre-reform mathematics achievement gap between disadvantaged and non-disadvantaged schools at sixth-grade entry. The reform is also associated with a small increase in students' self-reported readiness to succeed. These findings suggest that class size reduction, when targeted at the students expected to benefit most, produces effects that persist well beyond the early grades in which it was implemented.

detail.abstract: Strategic work-life balance (WLB) practices are increasingly recognized as organizational resources that may support employee well-being, workforce stability, and efficient use of operating resources. This study examined strategic WLB practices and perceived operating expense efficiency among non-military personnel in a Philippine defense institution. A quantitative descriptive-correlational design was employed, and data were collected through a validated structured questionnaire using a census of the accessible population. Descriptive statistics and Pearson's product-moment correlation were used to analyze the data. Respondents agreed that strategic WLB practices were present, with accessible leave benefits rated most favorably, while telecommuting access and program communication received the lowest assessments. They also viewed perceived operating expense efficiency favorably across recruitment and retention costs, absenteeism losses, and facility overhead expenses, with reduced absenteeism rated highest. A statistically significant moderate positive relationship was found between strategic WLB practices and perceived operating expense efficiency, indicating association rather than causation. The main implementation challenges involved limited managerial support, wellness funding, performance assessment, inconsistent application of flexible arrangements, technology, communication, staffing, policy clarity, and work-life boundaries. Accordingly, the study proposes clear telework guidelines, consistent WLB communication, supervisory accountability, wellness support, output-based performance standards, adequate technology and staffing, and protected work-life boundaries. These findings may guide institutional leaders in integrating WLB practices into workforce planning and resource management while maintaining employee well-being, operational accountability, and continuity of public service.

detail.abstract: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) account for more than 90 percent of businesses, 50 percent of GDP, and 80 percent of employment across sub-Saharan Africa, yet remain systematically excluded from national AI strategies. Through comparative policy analysis of AI strategies, TVET frameworks, and innovation funding mechanisms in Egypt, Kenya, Mauritius, Rwanda, and South Africa, this paper identifies three structural failures driving the AI skills gap facing African SMEs. They are AI strategies that acknowledge SMEs rhetorically but direct support toward startup-oriented innovation rather than operational adoption, TVET systems that lack applied, business-size-differentiated AI competencies, and innovation funding that finances technology acquisition without mandating workforce training. These failures reflect policy design choices rather than resource constraints and are manageable without new institutions. Simply by embedding SME-differentiated adoption roadmaps into existing strategies, integrating applied AI modules into TVET curricula via UNESCO-UNEVOC frameworks, and restructuring innovation grants to bundle technology with training. The paper situates these findings within the implementation window of the African Union's Continental AI Strategy, arguing that the next eighteen months are critical before exclusion becomes entrenched at continental scale.

detail.abstract: More advertising data can produce greater apparent precision under a mistaken independence assumption. Across a declared simulation grid, confirmed violations of nominal 95% coverage for impression-level Clopper-Pearson intervals rise from 11 of 36 scenarios with 100 users to 27 with 50,000. Approximate cluster intervals improve with user count but still violate nominal coverage in six of 36 scenarios even with 50,000 users. Public advertising logs show the reporting consequences. Accounting for users under the same Hoeffding procedure reduces sufficiently precise Criteo campaigns from 75 to five. In adjacent weeks, user-level Hoeffding intervals meet the tolerance for seven campaigns, and six subsequent observed rates fall outside them. Bounding user contributions improves precision while changing the measured rate. These findings support specifying the estimand, independence unit, tolerance, confidence, and transfer assumption whenever data are declared sufficient. Historical precision alone is not evidence of next-period agreement.

detail.abstract: In multistore retail settings, consumers may inspect products at one store and then decide whether to visit another based on realized and expected utility, potentially incurring search costs associated with travel time or transportation. To capture this sequential decision process and consumers' product choices across stores, we develop a hybrid search-and-choice model that integrates discrete choice with an endogenous sequential search framework. We derive closed-form expressions for the resulting choice probabilities and establish key structural properties of consumers' search and choice behavior. We then investigate several related operational problems, including assortment planning, price optimization, and model estimation. For assortment planning, we establish the NP-hardness of the problem, analyze the theoretical performance of markup-ordered assortments, and develop both a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (FPTAS) and a novel polynomial-time algorithm with a constantfactor approximation guarantee. For pricing, we show that adjusted markups are invariant across products within each store. Moreover, under a common price sensitivity within each store, we reduce the original high-dimensional multiproduct pricing problem to a one-dimensional optimization problem. For model estimation, we exploit the blockwise concavity of the log-likelihood function to develop efficient estimation procedures for different data structures. Extensive empirical validation using real-world data demonstrates that the proposed model outperforms benchmark models in terms of model fit and predictive accuracy for consumer choices, sales, and revenue. The results also show that ignoring consumers' hybrid search-and-choice behavior can lead to substantial losses.

detail.abstract: Purpose: The current study aims to identify the key drivers of impulse buying behaviour in the online fashion retail sector and additionally examine how the identified factors contribute to stimulate impulse based spontaneous purchase of Fashion Apparels online. Design/methodology/approach: The study adopts an Empirical approach with a quantitative research design using primary data collected through a structured questionnaire from 616 active fashion retail consumers identified through snowball sampling. Exploratory factor analysis was deployed to identify the underlying latent constructs driving impulse buying behaviour of Online Fashion retail Apparel. The approach of multiple linear regression analysis further facilitated the evaluation of the impact of the identified latent factors. Findings: The results show that personal situational factors together with psychological-emotional factors most strongly impact impulse buying behavior while product and fashion involvement and social influence , website platform features and promotional and marketing activities follow as less important factors. The factor of payment convenience exhibit weaker impacts on the impulse buying behaviour of Online Retail Fashion Apparel over other factors. The model successfully accounts for a explaining a substantial part (72.3%) of impulse buying behavior while demonstrating its statistical robustness for further inferential usability. Practical implications: The study makes a significant emphasis on the need for showcasing and promotional efforts for online fashion retailers suggesting a close focus on enhancing platform design, personalized recommendations, social media engagement, and emotionally appealing shopping experiences to stimulate impulsive purchases. Originality/value: Apart from contributing to the growing literature on digital consumer behaviour, the study gives immense insights on integrating technological, psychological, and situational drivers of impulse buying in the online fashion retail context.

detail.abstract: Average actual hours worked (AAHW) have declined across many advanced economies, affecting aggregate labor input and potential output. This paper examines the evolution of AAHW in Nordic countries between 2011 and 2022, with a focus on educational attainment and complementary ++gender, employment status, and citizenship. Using microdata from the European Union Labour Force Survey and a Shapley decomposition, the analysis shows that the decline in AAHW is primarily driven by reductions in hours among workers with lower and medium levels of educational attainment, used here as a proxy for skill levels. By contrast, highly educated workers work longer hours and their increasing share partly offsets the decline. Our decompositions show that this education-based result remains robust when worker groups are further split by age, gender and full-time/part-time status, and that most of the citizenship-related variation is concentrated among citizens, with non-citizen contributions generally smaller and often offsetting. Finland represents a temporary pandemic and post-pandemic exception, although the overall contribution of tertiary-educated workers remains positive. Supplementary evidence comparing desired and usual hours shows larger positive gaps among less-educated workers, while tertiary-educated workers in several countries appear closer to, or at times above, their preferred hours. These patterns are consistent with constraints on realized hours, stronger worker demand for hours, or both, but do not identify the underlying mechanism.

detail.abstract: Digital payment ecosystems increasingly combine card networks, mobile interfaces, automated fraud controls, authentication technologies, and artificial-intelligence-supported risk monitoring. In such environments, perceived transaction security is not only a technical attribute but also a trust-building signal. This study examines whether consumers' perceived transaction security is associated with trust in Mastercard-enabled payments in Bangladesh and whether trust functions as a mechanism linking security perceptions to cashless-payment intention. The study uses a quantitative, cross-sectional survey of adult consumers in Bangladesh with relevant Mastercard or Mastercard-enabled payment experience, using a five-point Likert instrument and a theory-driven structural model informed by Protection Motivation Theory (PMT) and trust theory. The study dataset contains 400 respondent IDs, of which 385 cases are fully populated and were retained for analysis; the remaining 15 rows are blank placeholders. All 385 retained cases passed the embedded attention check. Because the documented questionnaire operationalises transaction security and trust but does not provide validated AI-specific construct wording, AI is treated as an ecosystem context rather than as a causal latent variable. A reproducible variance-oriented analysis was conducted using construct scores, bootstrap inference, mediation analysis, measurement diagnostics, multicollinearity assessment, and 10-fold out-of-sample prediction. Transaction security was positively associated with trust (standardised β=0.313, p<.001), while trust was positively associated with cashless-payment intention (β=0.137, p=.007). The indirect effect through trust was 0.043 with a 95% bootstrap confidence interval [0.009, 0.085], indicating a statistically detectable but modest mediating mechanism. The measurement diagnostics simultaneously reveal an important qualification: Cronbach's alpha values for the three-item focal constructs are below conventional thresholds, while composite reliability is around or above .70 and AVE is slightly below .50 for transaction security and trust. Accordingly, the structural evidence should be interpreted as preliminary rather than as definitive causal validation. The study contributes a Bangladesh-specific security-to-trust pathway and identifies measurement refinement as a priority for future AI-enabled payment research.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence reaches occupations unevenly, and how exposed workers fare depends on which of their tasks remain with labor and on which jobs they can reach. I construct a complementarity-adjusted dynamic AI exposure index, C-DAIOE, that discounts technical exposure in the task contexts where human input remains valuable, and link it to Norwegian employer-employee registers for 2010-2024 and to an occupational mobility network estimated from pre-period worker transitions. Within firms, a one-standard-deviation increase in exposure is associated with 11 percent lower employment in an occupation, but only where task complementarity is low; raw exposure has no relationship with employment. The decline operates through fewer hires into exposed occupations rather than more exits from them. Across workers, direct exposure is associated with more occupation and employer switching, whereas exposure among the occupations a worker could move to is associated with less, and movers are more likely to enter less exposed, more complementary, and better-paid occupations, the more so when the destinations their occupation historically fed into are themselves less exposed. Exposure is not associated with short-run earnings growth.

detail.abstract: Digital transformation is increasingly central to economic development, public-service delivery, business competitiveness, and regional integration. Yet countries face uneven challenges in building digital infrastructure, widening affordable access, developing skills, protecting data, and connecting digital systems across borders. This paper examines how Malawi, Zambia, Mozambique, Tanzania, and Zimbabwe can cooperate to strengthen digital transformation across agriculture, health, education, financial services, trade, transport, manufacturing, public administration, and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The study uses a qualitative, comparative, desk-based design. It synthesize peer-reviewed studies published between 2018 and 2025 with national policy documents for the five countries and policy documents of the Southern African Development Community (SADC), the African Union, and the World Bank. The synthesis covers six connected areas: digital infrastructure, policy and data-governance cooperation, digital public infrastructure and connecting financial systems, cross-border trade and logistics, human capital and inclusion, and sectoral applications. It distinguishes carefully between regional policy commitments, documented implementation, and measured outcomes. The country-level evidence shows that all five countries already have national digital strategies or policies, but that they differ in legal coverage, institutional maturity, and implementation status. The regional problem is therefore the uneven alignment of national systems rather than the absence of national policy. On this basis the paper develops a Sub-Regional Digital Transformation Cooperation Framework built on six pillars, with an implementation pathway, a governance architecture that complements rather than replaces existing SADC and continental arrangements, a risk register, and indicators for monitoring and evaluation. The framework is an evidence-informed analytical and policy framework.

detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly contributes to activities through which human capabilities have traditionally been applied, developed, and demonstrated. This paper argues that the significance of this change lies not only in what AI can perform, but in how it can alter these functions differently: AI may improve performance or support learning while making observable output less informative about individual capability. Distinguishing the productive function of tasks from their developmental function, the paper examines how AI changes the relationship among task performance, capability formation, assessment, and degree signaling. It argues that higher education should increasingly emphasize domain understanding, problem formulation, transfer, adaptive expertise, critical evaluation, and judgment while distinguishing between independent and AI-augmented performance. The resulting challenge is to maintain alignment among learning design, assessment, and certification so that credentials remain credible signals of human capability. AI, therefore, does not eliminate the fundamental functions of higher education; it changes the conditions under which universities must develop and credibly demonstrate them.

detail.abstract: Background: The rapid growth of online food ordering and delivery platforms has significantly transformed the global food service industry. However, existing systems, particularly in developing countries, often suffer from poor usability, inefficient order management, limited real-time tracking, scalability challenges, and security vulnerabilities. These limitations reduce customer satisfaction and operational efficiency. Aim: To design, develop, and evaluate SmartBite, a secure, scalable, and user-friendly web-based online food ordering and delivery system that enhances customer convenience, improves restaurant operations, and ensures transparency through real-time GPS-based tracking.  Methods: SmartBite was developed using modern web technologies, including React.js for the frontend, Node.js and Express.js for backend services, and MongoDB for database management. Secure authentication was implemented using JSON Web Tokens (JWT), while Leaflet.js was used for GPS-based delivery tracking. The system was evaluated through unit testing, API validation, integration testing, performance assessment, and usability testing involving 20 participants. Key performance metrics included page load time, API success rate, authentication accuracy, and user satisfaction.  Results: System evaluation demonstrated 100% successful API response validation, secure authentication with 100% access control accuracy, and average page load times below 3 seconds under standard network conditions. Usability testing indicated high user acceptance, with 85% reporting ease of navigation, 78% expressing satisfaction with the real-time tracking feature, and 82% overall satisfaction. Integration testing revealed seamless frontend–backend communication without critical system failures, confirming system reliability and operational efficiency. Conclusion: SmartBite effectively addresses the limitations of conventional food delivery systems by providing a secure, transparent, and efficient web-based platform. The integration of modern web technologies and real-time tracking significantly enhances user experience, operational performance, and service transparency. The proposed system demonstrates strong potential for large-scale deployment and contributes to the advancement of digital transformation in food service ecosystems, particularly in developing regions.

detail.abstract: Investments in AI can improve worker productivity and output quality, but whether those gains reach the people organizations serve is less clear. In collaboration with the Somaliland Ministry of Health and an international development organization, we study the staggered rollout of a human-AI collaborative documentation system at Somaliland's largest public hospital. The physician-initiated, text-based design of this AI tool addresses local language constraints without relying on recorded conversations. Combining detailed patient visit records, clinical notes, and physician surveys, we estimate intent-to-treat (ITT) effects using a Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) difference-indifferences design. Our results show that AI availability substantially reduces service time and improves documentation quality. Despite concerns about adoption, we observe that even non-adopting physicians' humanwritten notes improve after AI exposure, consistent with learning benefits from using AI as a reference. Yet we find no corresponding overall improvement in patient waiting time or throughput. Departmental comparisons and queueing simulations highlight how persistent gaps in scheduling, patient flow management, and clinical availability can prevent faster service from improving access. This gap is especially consequential in developing economies, where hospitals may adopt advanced AI tools while still lacking basic practices such as appointment scheduling and patient flow management. Our findings suggest that health systems and development agencies seeking to expand access to care should complement AI deployment with improvements in basic operations and incentives.

detail.abstract: Background/Context. Videoconference fatigue is well documented, but its consequences for continued use intention remain unclear. Research Problem/Gap. Conservation of resources (COR) theory and the expectationconfirmation model (ECM) are rarely integrated, and the operating characteristics of such a model at realistic sample sizes are unknown. Research in this area typically uses a few hundred cases and three-item scales. Objective. The study specifies an integrated COR-ECM model of videoconferencing continuance and evaluates its estimability by simulation. Method. A data-generating process was specified from theory with coefficients fixed in advance. Five hundred independent samples were drawn in each cell of a fully crossed design (n = 200 to 600; loading λ = 0.70 to 0.85), giving 4,500 datasets estimated by PLS-SEM, and two misspecifications were introduced. Key Findings. Measured against the composite value PLS-SEM targets, recovery was close to exact: the largest absolute bias was 0.005 and coverage lay between 0.946 and 0.976. Measured against the latent coefficient, the same estimates show a 15.4% shortfall on the satisfaction to continuance path, widening to 29% at λ = 0.70. That gap is an estimand effect, not estimator error. Precision improved with sample size and loading. An unmeasured common cause produced a spurious path of 0.20 that no diagnostic flagged. Contribution/Implication. The study provides a fully specified model, quantifies the gap between latent coefficients and the composite values PLS-SEM estimates, and shows a conventional workflow misses a plausible misspecification. Reported coefficients should not be read as latent effects, and measurement diagnostics cannot substitute for safeguards against confounding.

detail.abstract: Hackathons are often assessed through immediate outputs such as attendance, ideas, and prototypes. These measures do not establish whether an output becomes a maintained digital product or what resources are consumed after the event. This article synthesizes selected literature on hackathon continuity, open innovation, experimentation, and software technical debt to clarify the lifecycle-cost question and identify an operational research agenda. It distinguishes event expenditure from validation, remediation and integration, deployment, operation, and exit costs; separates observed expenditure from forecasts; and explains why discontinued outputs must remain visible in cost reporting. Its contribution is therefore a transparent conceptual and methodological proposal intended to support subsequent empirical testing, not a validated instrument or evidence that hackathons are more or less cost-effective than other innovation approaches.

detail.abstract: Context: Health systems face a paradox. Aging populations, advanced therapeutics, and long term needs expand demand for high value care while large financial stocks coexist with incomplete service coverage and widespread financial hardship. The article examines whether this mismatch reflects a circulatory pathology of capital allocation in care intensive sectors where biological vulnerability and human dignity are most exposed. Methods: This paper uses a structured conceptual synthesis for theory building rather than statistical estimation. It integrates research on precautionary saving, institutional trust, health financing, accreditation, real world evidence, and programmable financial governance under protocols for source selection, bibliographic verification, and bias control. Interdisciplinary convergence is treated as theoretical triangulation, not empirical proof. Findings: The synthesis develops financial venous stasis and thrombosis as a bounded theory building metaphor. Care cost insecurity is its proposed behavioral hinge. Capital may pool for future security and care assurance as well as yield. When prudent preservation against aging, illness, and care uncertainty scales through institutional routines and risk controls, it may harden into systemic low flow that monetary expansion alone may not resolve. The response is an institutional treatment architecture for financial thrombolysis. It places a clinical core without profit distributions within an auditable phased CeFi-to-DeFi governance structure supported by accreditation, real world evidence, and transparent flow protocols. Conclusions: The framework does not claim empirical validation. It is a falsifiable health policy agenda dependent on pilot testing and assessable through clinical outcomes, patient experience, compliance integrity, cash flow durability, equity effects, and transparent social allocation. Its central contribution reframes capital not as a scarce resource to be rationed but as a circulatory medium whose movement may be impaired. It tests whether usable channels can restore circulation and convert defensive preservation into measurable care capacity that protects dignity without penalizing capital.

detail.abstract: While orthodox development economics frequently models poverty alleviation through human capital accumulation, asset building, and market integration, it routinely commits a fundamental operational error: it presumes an unexamined baseline of functional literacy, cognitive bandwidth, and administrative eligibility. In From Subsistence to Holistic Security (Rumbaoa, 2026), the Sequential Mobility Model (SMM) formalized the progressive phasing required to transition vulnerable households from subsistence stabilization to intergenerational wealth creation. This paper provides the operational precursor to that framework by formalizing Phase 0: The Pre-Mobility Subsistence Stratum. We establish a diagnostic taxonomy of precarity across three distinct structural tiers: Level 1 (Severe Cognitive Bandwidth Depletion and Illiteracy), Level 2 (Oral-Receptive Illiteracy with Intact Auditory Scaffolding), and Level 3 (Functional Literacy Constrained by Credentialing Asymmetry). We demonstrate that conventional interventions fail because of an interface mismatch, imposing high-compliance textual burdens on cognitively tax-saturated actors. Furthermore, we model the post-Level 3 labor market entry condition as Survival-Driven Labor Price-Taking, proving that strategic labor bargaining cannot emerge until surplus liquidity and modular human capital accumulate in SMM Phase 3. By charting the transition mechanics across these strata-incorporating caloric priming, dual-code phonetic scaffolding, and alternative accreditation systems (ALS/ETEEAP)-this paper delivers an actionable, empirically grounded policy framework for de-risking the foundational threshold of human mobility.

detail.abstract:
Enterprise artificial intelligence is being procured as if it were ordinary software. It is not. Once an AI system begins accumulating an organization's prompts, memories, embeddings, workflow definitions, agent configurations, and feedback, and begins mediating decisions, documents, code, and customer relationships, the organization is no longer buying functionality. It is transferring part of its cognitive infrastructure to an outside company. This paper argues that the most serious enterprise AI risk is not an incorrect answer but the gradual loss of the ability to operate, preserve institutional knowledge, defend decisions, and leave, without a provider the organization does not control.

The paper makes three contributions. First, building on recent scholarship that describes AI as cognitive infrastructure, it defines enterprise-created state and cognitive dependency in the enterprise buyer-provider relationship, as distinct from the data and service dependencies that existing governance regimes address. Second, it examines AI risk-management standards (NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001), financial-sector operational-resilience rules (including the EU Digital Operational Resilience Act), cloud-switching law (the EU Data Act), and the algorithmic-monoculture literature, and identifies what each leaves unaddressed when the dependency is cognitive. Third, it presents FORCE, a buyer-side governance framework organized around five dimensions (Fiduciary Custody, Operational Continuity, Resilience Against Monoculture, Control and Organizational Autonomy, and Egress and Exit), three board decision gates, twelve non-negotiable provider requirements, a consequence-based deployment architecture, and a five-level evidence scorecard with a weakest-link scoring rule. As external triangulation rather than validation, the paper records that in the weeks around FORCE's publication on 30 September 2026, senior figures in technology, finance, and banking supervision independently articulated individual elements of the framework, while none addressed exit. The paper closes with limitations, a research agenda, and a note on a forthcoming companion framework for individuals.

detail.abstract: Purpose. Enterprise transformations are widely reported to underperform their stated objectives, with frequently cited failure estimates of around 70% (Kotter, 1995; Beer & Nohria, 2000). This paper argues that a substantial share of that underperformance originates in flawed pre-investment diagnostic research, and examines two failure modes: the syndication fallacy, in which repeated copies of a single narrative are mistaken for empirical consensus, and causal conflation, in which surface symptoms are treated as root causes. It introduces the Epistemic Standard, a rule-governed research framework for establishing diagnostic ground truth before transformation capital is committed. Design / conceptual framework. The framework enforces three governance protocols: (1) a non-collapsible seven-level causal hierarchy-root cause, problem, challenge, complexity, scenario, symptom, business impact; (2) origin-based independence counting with mandatory epistemic labels (FACT, EVIDENCE, INFERENCE, HYPOTHESIS) and explicit disclosure of contested evidence; and (3) a technology-honesty rule paired with an "HR-Alone Will Fail" escalation where root causes sit outside the HR function. The framework gives CHROs, transformation leaders and boards an auditable evidence ledger rather than a narrative summary, reducing the risk of premature technology commitments. Originality / value. The paper separates problem diagnosis from solution advocacy, proposing a vendor-neutral diagnostic architecture distinct from both unconstrained generative synthesis and implementation-linked advisory models. detail.abstract:
Trust in a signed document’s integrity rests on the belief that its signature cannot be forged. It rests on assumptions about the algorithm, which can fail. For a document that must be trusted for decades after signing, the question is what will still support the belief then, and who keeps that support. For the UK e-Apostille, a notary in England and Wales can obtain one for a client’s power of attorney but cannot say how long anyone, including the notary, can convincingly show that the document is unchanged. A sufficiently capable quantum computer could remove the basis for that belief in current digital signatures within the document’s life, and such machines’ spread matters as much as the date. An issued e-Apostille keeps its original signatures. The Article 7 check of the Apostille Convention compares the certificate’s particulars with the register, not the document. Two recent texts address the question: one on EU and German civil procedure (Hoeren and Pinelli, 2025), one a presentation leaving it to lawyers (Kesterson, Lightowler and Mason, 2025). Neither treats the UK e-Apostille.

This essay separates two functions: checking an apostille certificate’s particulars and binding the certificate to the original electronic document. In eleven public texts, the only passage naming an actor for the second is a non-binding Hague Conference (HCCH) principle that Competent Authorities preserve signature validity over time. No UK text read says that the Legalisation Office has adopted it for issued e-Apostilles. UK trust services law and European standards describe preservation, but the provisions read oblige no one to apply it. The essay sets out the cost and payer of six options, and which reach issued documents. It aims to contribute to the discussion where technology meets law, and invites legal practitioners and notaries into it: who should carry the duty?

detail.abstract: As the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools is becoming increasingly common in all aspects of research, there is a growing debate as to how and how much such tools will influence theorizing as well. In this viewpoint article, I discuss three plausible scenarios that could arise from a combination of efficiency pressures, practice shifts and collective choices: (i) theorizing will remain human-centric while empirical research will be AI-centric; (ii) theorizing will become more data-driven and evidence-based thanks to AI, crowding out paradigm-based theorizing; and (iii) theorizing will be professionalized as an AI-enhanced workflow. I compare characteristics and major implications of each scenario, and reflect on skills we scholars need to develop to effectively theorize with and without AI going forward.

detail.abstract: In today's rapidly advancing technological landscape, many companies are struggling to break free from their reliance on outsourcing. For example, the automotive industry has long relied on outsourcing software technology, resulting in a lack of core technical expertise. One reason why this problem persists despite recognition is that the organizational mechanisms behind this reliance on outsourcing are not fully understood. This research aims to bridge that knowledge gap. We posed the research question: "When introducing innovative technologies, are frontline employees or managers more concerned about a lack of knowledge within their company?" The case study focused on the software-defined vehicle (SDV) development department at Honda Motor Co., Ltd. in Japan. We comprehensively evaluated expectations for improved development speed, SDV-related factors (SDV technology, customer needs, company knowledge), and general organizational factors (ideas, approval process, innovation culture, risk management, decision-making) among 1,374 regular employees and 170 middle managers in this department. The results revealed that while employees on the front lines perceive their company's knowledge as effective, managers perceive a lack of it. Thus, there is a serious perception gap regarding the company's knowledge between frontline employees and decision-makers, and it can be inferred that outsourcing is perceived as necessary primarily from a management perspective. Existing literature on the introduction of innovative technologies has shown that employees feel fear, while managers are eager to adopt them. However, this study showed that in technology-based companies, employees are confident in their on-the-ground knowledge and are willing to quickly conduct experiments toward innovation. Similar to Peter Drucker's adage, "Culture eats strategy for breakfast," the results of this study suggest the existence of "Culture eats technology for breakfast." No matter how advanced the technology, it will not function effectively without the organizational culture and processes to leverage it.

detail.abstract: Managers routinely compare units that differ in how much they do and how well they do it, such as products with many reviews or high ratings and salespeople with many accounts or valuable ones. This article proposes Perf, the total multiplied by the average, as a single metric for such comparisons. The formula is identical to the exergy indicator that Prathap developed for research evaluation. The main contribution is a set of extensions for business data. These include a reference point for ratings, a premium on quality calibrated with one question, an evidence-weighted Net Promoter Score, a customer-base Perf for evaluating companies and an uncertainty band. A research agenda follows.

detail.abstract:
Background: Atrial fibrillation (AF) can be triggered by atrial ectopic beats, but ectopics are too common to be  good risk markers on their own.

Methods: We used artificial intelligence (AI) to identify atrial ectopic types associated with AF on ambulatory ECG. We included 6,103 patients (age 69±13, 44% male) with ≥14 days of monitoring, ≥100 atrial ectopics and no AF≥30s in the first 48h. Beats were detected and classified using an FDA-approved AI algorithm (DeepRhythmAI, MEDICALgorithmics). We extracted ≤100 random atrial ectopic beats per patient (561,602 beats), and trained a convolutional neural network to measure 23 morphologic and interval-based characteristics.  We derived atrial ectopic beat types with a Gaussian mixture model, and tested whether the type mix in the first 48h predicted AF≥30s during the remainder of monitoring (≤30 days) using Cox models adjusted for age, sex, atrial ectopic frequency, and mean sinus heart rate. 

Findings: We identified six different atrial ectopic beat types; two predominated: “typical post-sinus ectopics” (47.5%) and “early post-sinus ectopics” (40.1%). AF occurred in 934 (15.3%) of patients. Early post-sinus ectopics, with short coupling intervals and long pauses, were associated with AF (HR 1.06, 95%CI 1.03-1.09/10% increase in proportion). Each additional type also predicted AF (HR 1.20 95%CI 1.13-1.28/additional type). There were substantial differences in AF occurrence in patients with different atrial ectopic types; in patients with 50-249 atrial ectopics/24h, AF occurred in 16.1% (95%CI 10.9–21.4%) when >75% were early post sinus ectopics versus 5.3% (95%CI 3.3–7.4%) when >75% were typical. Very high AF rates, 29.1% (95%CI 22.8-35.4%), were seen with >75% early post-sinus, ≥1000 atrial ectopics/24h, and ≥3 types.

Interpretation: A novel AI pipeline identified an atrial ectopic type (≈40% of ectopics) associated with AF occurrence, and showed that having several types is also associated with AF risk.

detail.abstract:
Background: Existing small cell lung cancer (SCLC) prognostic models often incorporate treatment information unavailable at diagnosis. We developed and externally validated pretreatment models using routinely available variables and assessed their cross-national transportability.

Methods: We analyzed 10,291 US Flatiron patients (training, n = 7,204; internal validation, n = 3,087) and 970 Chinese patients for external validation. Across 20 imputed datasets, XGBoost used 12 candidate predictors, whereas least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-Cox included predictors selected in ≥50% of imputations. Performance was assessed using Harrell’s C-index, time-dependent areas under the curve (AUCs) at 1, 3, and 5 years, calibration, and decision-curve analysis. Comparators were Veterans Administration Lung Study Group (VALSG) stage and an operationalized Vincent/Royal Marsden index. Exploratory analyses examined cross-national predictor effects and 1-year model updating.

Findings: LASSO retained seven predictors: stage, albumin, age, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, and neutrophil count. Stage was dominant in both models (pooled Cox hazard ratio, 2·578; 95% CI, 2·414–2·754; mean XGBoost gain, 47·4%). External 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUCs were 0·726 (95% CI, 0·688–0·769), 0·684 (0·629–0·740), and 0·769 (0·664–0·874) for XGBoost and 0·719, 0·687, and 0·749 for LASSO-Cox. Both models provided net benefit over clinically relevant threshold ranges and generally outperformed VALSG stage and the Vincent/Royal Marsden index. In China, baseline-hazard updating reduced the 1-year inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted Brier score from 0·206 to 0·155.

Interpretation: This study developed and cross-nationally validated XGBoost- and LASSO-Cox-based SCLC prognostic models using variables available at diagnosis. Together with a web-based calculator, these models support pretreatment risk assessment, but require local calibration assessment and further validation before clinical implementation.

detail.abstract:
Background: Preoperative identification of occult high-risk pathological features could inform surgery for early-stage lung adenocarcinoma, but imaging-AI approaches often require raw images, segmentation, and specialised infrastructure. We developed PATHWISE to combine semantic information in routine CT reports with structured clinicoradiological data.

Methods: In this multicentre diagnostic prediction study, PATHWISE integrated large-language-model interpretation of CT reports, structured-variable XGBoost, and text-based logistic regression through probability fusion. Models were developed in the Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital retrospective cohort and evaluated without refitting in two external retrospective cohorts and a prospective cohort. A paired multi-reader study assessed six thoracic surgeons before and after PATHWISE assistance. The primary outcome was a composite of high-risk pathological subtype, spread through air spaces, visceral pleural invasion, or lymphovascular invasion.

Findings: Of 2591 screened patients, 2026 were enrolled and 2019 were model-evaluable. For the primary composite outcome, PATHWISE achieved an AUROC of 0·818 (95% CI 0·793–0·843) in development, 0·802 (0·767–0·833) in pooled external validation, and 0·896 (0·832–0·954) in prospective validation with the Qwen3.7-Max backbone. In 202 reader-study cases, assistance increased mean accuracy from 67·4% to 85·9% and mean AUROC from 0·674 to 0·860. Prospective component-endpoint estimates for visceral pleural and lymphovascular invasion were imprecise because of sparse events.

Interpretation: Routine CT reports contain clinically useful preoperative risk information. PATHWISE showed multicentre and prospective discrimination and improved surgeon interpretation in an offline reader study, but external validation beyond Chinese-language reports and prospective workflow-embedded evaluation are needed before clinical adoption.

detail.abstract: Quantitative easing (QE) creates bank deposits when the Federal Reserve buys securities from non-banks, and this new money enters the banking system at a few primary dealers. I measure each bank's and county's exposure to these points of entry and show that it predicts deposit growth when the Fed is buying but not between programs. Controlling for asset-side QE exposure, deposit-channel exposure predicts additional lending and reaches far more banks. Within banks, lending rises more in exposed counties, favoring mortgages over small-business loans. Exposure also raises non-tradable employment and house prices in both QE episodes. Where money is created matters.
